title: Inside Herta's Cadillac F1 audition
raw_summary: Colton Herta might still somehow be one superlicence point short of a Formula 1 superlicence after a bizarre error, but his latest Cadillac F1 outing was an important audition to replace Valtteri Bottas next year. An incorrect calculation of his superlicence points (verified at the time by the FIA) means Herta erroneously thought completing 30 laps in his fifth FP1 outing of the season in Mexico would be enough to take him to the 40-point threshold required to finally earn him the superlicence he’s been chasing for years.
summary: Colton Herta might still somehow be one superlicence point short of a Formula 1 superlicence after a bizarre error, but his latest Cadillac F1 outing was an important audition to replace Valtteri Bottas next year.
article_paragraphs: Colton Herta might still somehow be one superlicence point short of a Formula 1 superlicence after a bizarre error, but his latest Cadillac F1 outing was an important audition to replace Valtteri Bottas next year.

An incorrect calculation of his superlicence points (verified at the time by the FIA) means Herta erroneously thought completing 30 laps in his fifth FP1 outing of the season in Mexico would be enough to take him to the 40-point threshold required to finally earn him the superlicence he’s been chasing for years.
“I was literally walking to go do the media stuff [after FP2], that was like the first time I had heard about it,” Herta said on Friday evening.
“Obviously, we were still doing our meetings and whatnot, so I haven't talked to anybody about it. As far as I was concerned, going into the weekend, if I did 100km here, I would have 40 [points].

“So, I'm not sure what's changed, or why stuff has changed, or if it even has. I have to wait and see. I think a lot of the people that I want to talk to about this are still in the meeting. Maybe I'll have a little bit more clarity this evening.”

Cadillac has gone beyond the mandated four rookie practice outings and given Herta a fifth session in Mexico to get him an extra point. Cadillac will run him again to get the final point, and had planned to anyway before the bizarre calculation error emerged.

But his Mexico outing wasn’t a case of Herta simply cruising around to get the mandated 100km of running to get the point. He was given an extensive programme that wasn’t too dissimilar from Perez's, his 2027 team-mate, should he secure Bottas’s race seat.
Herta’s FP1 starts with an 11-lap stint on the hard tyres with a best lap of 1m22.452s, 1.067s slower than Perez’s on the same tyres.

raw_title: Acosta wins chaotic Sepang MotoGP sprint
title: Acosta wins chaotic Sepang MotoGP sprint
raw_summary: Pedro Acosta claimed victory in a bizarre Sepang MotoGP sprint that was threatened by rain late on. Acosta came out on top of a four-way battle for the race win, prevailing by 0.578s over Marc Marquez, who increased his championship chances with second place.
summary: Pedro Acosta claimed victory in a bizarre Sepang MotoGP sprint that was threatened by rain late on. Acosta came out on top of a four-way battle for the race win, prevailing by 0.578s over Marc Marquez, who increased his championship chances with second place.
article_paragraphs: Pedro Acosta claimed victory in a bizarre Sepang MotoGP sprint that was threatened by rain late on.
Acosta came out on top of a four-way battle for the race win, prevailing by 0.578s over Marc Marquez, who increased his championship chances with second place.
Marquez is now 19 points up on the absent Jorge Martin, and 52 points clear of Marco Bezzecchi.
His brother Alex Marquez had got the start from pole position and led uncontested for four laps until he slid out of the race lead at Turn 14.
The lead was then inherited by Ai Ogura, who had moved up to second place after an aggressive opening corner tussle with Marc.

Spots of rain meant the white flag came out on lap two, allowing riders to swap bikes - with Jack Miller immediately prepared to take the gamble, but his Pramac Yamaha team not ready with his second bike, which frustrated him to no end.

Iker Lecuona, Joan Mir and Franco Morbidelli were the first group to come in and successfully switch on lap five, but were setting times almost 10 seconds off the leaders’ pace, with Maverick Vinales the only other rider electing to change towards the end of the race.
In the tricky conditions the top four bunched up, Ogura managing to hold off the challenges until Acosta attacked with three laps to spare.

title: Hyundai IONIQ 3 Named European Car of the Year 2027 Finalist
raw_summary: SEOUL/OFFENBACH — Hyundai Motor’s all-electric IONIQ 3 has been named one of seven finalists for the European Car of the Year 2027 award. Selected by an independent jury of automotive journalists from across Europe, the nomination places IONIQ 3 among the contenders for one of Europe’s most established automotive awards. The winner will be announced on 8 January 2027 at the Brussels Motor Show. Designed in Europe and produced at Hyundai Motor Türkiye’s İzmit plant, IONIQ 3 has been developed specifically for European customers. The fully electric compact hatchback combines Hyundai’s distinctive ‘Art of Steel’ design language, a spacious interior and intuitive technology with a driving range of up to 497 km (WLTP) in the Long Range version. With a starting price below €30,000 across European markets, IONIQ 3 aims to make electric mobility accessible to a broader range of customers.

article_paragraphs: SEOUL/OFFENBACH — Hyundai Motor’s all-electric IONIQ 3 has been named one of seven finalists for the European Car of the Year 2027 award. Selected by an independent jury of automotive journalists from across Europe, the nomination places IONIQ 3 among the contenders for one of Europe’s most established automotive awards. The winner will be announced on 8 January 2027 at the Brussels Motor Show.

Designed in Europe and produced at Hyundai Motor Türkiye’s İzmit plant, IONIQ 3 has been developed specifically for European customers. The fully electric compact hatchback combines Hyundai’s distinctive ‘Art of Steel’ design language, a spacious interior and intuitive technology with a driving range of up to 497 km (WLTP) in the Long Range version. With a starting price below €30,000 across European markets, IONIQ 3 aims to make electric mobility accessible to a broader range of customers.

“Being named a finalist for European Car of the Year is important recognition for IONIQ 3 and for the work that has gone into its development. We set out to create an electric car designed around the needs of European customers, combining distinctive design with class-leading aerodynamics, strong driving range and exceptional interior space, together with advanced technology at an accessible price. The response from customers has been very encouraging, with orders already exceeding our initial expectations. This nomination reflects the strength of that overall package and our ambition to make electric mobility both desirable and practical for more people.” —Christopher McKinnon, Vice President, Head of Product and Product Director Office for Europe at Hyundai Motor Europe.

IONIQ 3 combines several class-leading features that address key requirements of European customers. Its aerodynamic design contributes to driving efficiency, while its spacious interior offers the practicality of a larger vehicle despite its compact exterior dimensions. Intuitive technology supports everyday usability, and accessible pricing makes electric mobility available to a broader range of customers.

The European Car of the Year award is an independent automotive competition established in 1964. Its international jury consists of 65 automotive journalists from across Europe, who evaluate eligible new vehicles based on criteria including design, innovation, performance, value for money and market positioning.

Seven finalists are selected from the initial list of candidates. Following further evaluation and voting, the overall winner of the 2027 award will be announced on 8 January 2027 at the Brussels Motor Show.

title: Forgotten Australian Supercar: The 1988 Giocattolo Group B
raw_summary: This is an original Giocattolo Group B, it’s an Australian supercar from the late-1980s with a mid-mounted Holden V8 and it was faster from 0-62 mph than both the Porsche 930 and the Ferrari Testarossa. Just 15 examples of the Group B would be built, around 12-13 are believed to have survived, and they’re among the most collectible Australian-built cars ever made – the problem for most enthusiasts is finding one for sale.

article_paragraphs: This is an original Giocattolo Group B, it’s an Australian supercar from the late-1980s with a mid-mounted Holden V8 and it was faster from 0-62 mph than both the Porsche 930 and the Ferrari Testarossa.

Just 15 examples of the Group B would be built, around 12-13 are believed to have survived, and they’re among the most collectible Australian-built cars ever made – the problem for most enthusiasts is finding one for sale.

Between 1986 and 1989, a small company called Giocattolo Motori of Caloundra, on Queensland’s Sunshine Coast, built 15 supercars based on brand new Alfa Romeo Sprints. The production cars had a Holden V8 where the rear seats had been, Kevlar fenders, and a small bottle of Bundaberg Rum with two shot glasses in the toolkit. Probably because after your first drive, you might need a couple of stiff drinks. The car’s model name was “Group B” and Giocattolo, the company name, is Italian for “toy.”

This is an original Giocattolo Group B, it’s an Australian supercar from the late-1980s with a mid-mounted Holden V8 and it was faster from 0-62 mph than both the Porsche 930 and the Ferrari Testarossa.

At the Paris Motor Show in October of 1982, Alfa Romeo showed the Alfasud Sprint 6C, a rally prototype for the new Group B category in global rally. It had a 2.5 liter V6 behind the front seats, sending power to the rear wheels via a ZF 5-speed gearbox of the type used in the Lancia 037 . Alfa couldn’t afford to build it as a homologation/production model, and sadly, the project was cancelled in 1983.

On the other side of the world in Australia, a man named Paul Halstead had made his money in IT recruitment and then opened The Toy Shop, a Sydney dealership selling De Tomasos , Ferraris , Lamborghinis , and Porsches . For a time he also exported Australian-built 351 cubic inch (5.8 liter) Ford Cleveland V8s to Italy for De Tomaso.
Barry Lock was a Queensland-based former McLaren Formula 1 engineer who built Kaditcha racing cars, and the two men knew each other well as Lock had built Halstead’s Pantera race car.

Halstead set out to make a road-going version of the cancelled 6C. He started from a production Alfa Romeo Sprint because of regulations – as Lock later explained, every door handle and lock on an all-new car would have needed Australian Design Rules (ADR) approval, and the Sprint already had all those boxes ticked.

title: Toyota & Waymo Advance Autonomous Driving Collaboration for Safer Streets and Freedom of Movement for All
raw_summary: Toyota Motor Corporation (“Toyota”) and Waymo today announced the next phase of their autonomous driving collaboration, in pursuit of a world with safer streets and freedom of movement for all. Building on the preliminary agreement announced in April 2025, Toyota and Waymo will begin initial operations to test and validate an autonomous Toyota bZ4X fleet in Japan in 2027, with deployment to the United Kingdom and other Waymo-serviced markets planned for the following years. This partnership marks a major milestone in the expansion of Japan’s first fully autonomous ride-hailing service using high-volume, domestically manufactured vehicles.

Building on the preliminary agreement announced in April 2025, Toyota and Waymo will begin initial operations to test and validate an autonomous Toyota bZ4X fleet in Japan in 2027, with deployment to the United Kingdom and other Waymo-serviced markets planned for the following years.
article_paragraphs: Toyota Motor Corporation (“Toyota”) and Waymo today announced the next phase of their autonomous driving collaboration, in pursuit of a world with safer streets and freedom of movement for all.

Building on the preliminary agreement announced in April 2025, Toyota and Waymo will begin initial operations to test and validate an autonomous Toyota bZ4X fleet in Japan in 2027, with deployment to the United Kingdom and other Waymo-serviced markets planned for the following years. This partnership marks a major milestone in the expansion of Japan’s first fully autonomous ride-hailing service using high-volume, domestically manufactured vehicles.

Toyota will build the vehicles at its Takaoka plant in Toyota City, Aichi Prefecture, Japan. The entire process will take place under one roof, from assembling the base vehicle to integrating Waymo’s AV hardware.

By pairing Toyota’s global manufacturing and vehicle development expertise with Waymo’s fully autonomous technology, the companies will accelerate scaling safety-validated Level 4 autonomous vehicles globally — helping provide people with transit that reduces human-error accidents, and opening up freedom of movement for those who can’t easily get around.

Beyond safety, the custom-outfitted bZ4X is designed for comfort and greater accessibility. Generous rear legroom and features such as automatic doors, a power liftgate, and ambient lighting will provide seamless entry and exit for riders.

Toyota and Waymo will continue to explore the future of autonomous driving technology for personally owned Toyota vehicles. Alongside Woven by Toyota, they will also explore additional initiatives that support their shared goal of fewer road safety incidents, including how insights from Waymo’s real-world operations, data-driven intelligence, and technology could holistically improve safety for other road users.

“Toyota’s commitment to zero traffic accidents resonates deeply with us at Waymo, and we’re proud to work together toward safer roads for all,” said Dmitri Dolgov, co-CEO of Waymo. “In areas where Waymo operates, we’ve demonstrated that we are up to 20x safer than human drivers when it comes to serious crash injuries, and our partnership with Toyota will help us bring the safety and convenience of autonomous driving to more people around the world, including key international markets like Japan. We chose Toyota because of our respect for the legendary safety, reliability, and quality of their vehicles, and we look forward to deepening our collaboration as we scale our fully autonomous Waymo Driver technology globally.”

“We are deeply grateful that Waymo, which helped pioneer fully autonomous driving technology, has chosen Toyota as its partner,” said Hiroki Nakajima, member of the board of directors and executive vice president of Toyota. “Safety technology makes the biggest difference when it reaches as many people as possible. This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still. No single company can achieve the goal of zero traffic accidents alone, but with partners like Waymo, we will get there one step at a time.”

raw_title: The Share of Solar Generation with Co-located Battery Storage Is Increasing
title: The Share of Solar Generation with Co-located Battery Storage Is Increasing
raw_summary: Utility-scale solar developers are increasingly co-locating battery storage with new solar photovoltaic capacity. As of September 2026, over 16% of new utility-scale solar capacity added this year is co-located with operable battery storage, compared with 2% in 2017, according to data reported to EIA by operators. Reported plans for solar additions scheduled to come online in the last three months of this year show that the share with co-located battery storage could increase to 19% this year. Longer-term plans indicate that this trend will continue, with the portion increasing to more than 30% in plans submitted for 2027 and 2028.
summary: Utility-scale solar developers are increasingly co-locating battery storage with new solar photovoltaic capacity. As of September 2026, over 16% of new utility-scale solar capacity added this year is co-located with operable battery storage, compared with 2% in 2017, according to data reported to EIA by operators.
article_paragraphs: Utility-scale solar developers are increasingly co-locating battery storage with new solar photovoltaic capacity. As of September 2026, over 16% of new utility-scale solar capacity added this year is co-located with operable battery storage, compared with 2% in 2017, according to data reported to EIA by operators.

Reported plans for solar additions scheduled to come online in the last three months of this year show that the share with co-located battery storage could increase to 19% this year. Longer-term plans indicate that this trend will continue, with the portion increasing to more than 30% in plans submitted for 2027 and 2028.

When operators co-locate battery storage with solar, they can direct solar electricity output to the grid or to the battery, depending on the wholesale prices. Wholesale prices in regions with large solar participation tend to fall when solar contributions are high and rise as they decrease. Plants with both solar and battery storage can manage the combined output of their generating resources to maximize their value in a changing wholesale price environment.

We publish unit-level generator inventory data based on our annual and monthly data collections, including information on design attributes for all utility-scale plants. Although battery storage and solar units at the same plant often enter commercial service at different times, the EIA-860 and EIA-860M data collection program tracks these developments and provides a monthly summary that can be used to identify co-located technologies.

Southwest states have higher-than-average solar capacity shares relative to their total generating capacity and also have higher levels of co-located utility-scale solar and battery capacity. As of September, 13% of the total U.S. utility-scale generating capacity is solar photovoltaic, and 18% of that is co-located with battery storage. The share of solar generation co-located with battery capacity in California, Arizona, New Mexico, and Nevada is more than double the national average.

title: HomePower 1000 Plus v2: Portable Power Put To Use
raw_summary: I have been using the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 in a wide range of applications over the past few months around my apartment in Queens, NY. The flexibility and portability make it especially useful for people living in apartments. I had previously written about the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 when it launched. You can read more about the technical specifications in that article . Overall, the battery charged in about an hour. It starts charging at a little over 1000 W and then drops to a little over 800 watts as it charges. The first thing I plugged into the battery was a fan, which used about 50 watts. summary: I have been using the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 in a wide range of applications over the past few months around my apartment in Queens, NY. The flexibility and portability make it especially useful for people living in apartments. I had previously written about the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 when it launched.
article_paragraphs: I have been using the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 in a wide range of applications over the past few months around my apartment in Queens, NY. The flexibility and portability make it especially useful for people living in apartments. I had previously written about the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 when it launched. You can read more about the technical specifications in that article .

Overall, the battery charged in about an hour. It starts charging at a little over 1000 W and then drops to a little over 800 watts as it charges. The first thing I plugged into the battery was a fan, which used about 50 watts. Then I plugged in my laptop, which charged at another 50 watts. I was able to work comfortably for a day off the battery with capacity to spare.

Keeping on the cool side, the battery was easily able to run my 12,000 BTU window air conditioner on a warmer day. Being in a century-old pre-war building, insulation could leave something to be desired. In addition, my corner apartment with large windows and 10-foot ceilings contributes to the load. Air conditioners can be a challenge to power, as the power consumption tends to spike when the compressor kicks in, but it did not pose a challenge to the battery. On a day in the mid-80’s (Fahrenheit), the battery was able to keep the indoor temperature in the mid-70’s all day with capacity to spare. Also, as my wife likes plugging her 1750 W clothes iron into the same circuit as the air conditioner, adding the battery could reduce the potential to trip the breaker when the compressor kicks in. It would be useful to maintain comfort during a power outage.

In terms of keeping things cool, the battery tends to use a little over 3% of its capacity per hour on my high-efficiency 14.1 cubic foot Midea refrigerator during the day with the door opening periodically. With the door staying shut, it would be closer to 2% per hour. That could potentially keep food from spoiling for a couple of days during an outage. While Jackery makes the FridgeGuard specifically for this application, the Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 could come in handy for added capacity during an emergency.

The battery would also come in handy for people with fish tanks to keep the pumps running during a power outage. I have an aquaponics setup with a few small fish to grow herbs and start seeds in the Spring. The battery can easily run the filters, pumps and heaters, as well as the powerful lights for the plants. However, for someone with exotic fish in a saltwater aquarium, battery backup could be essential to keeping the fish alive during a power disruption.

In addition, I was able to run my Vitamix blender with the HomePower 1000 Plus v2. The powerful motor can draw over 1000 W, but it doesn’t take long to blend up a smoothie or frozen beverage. As such, you could easily make frozen margaritas at a backyard party using the battery to power the blender.

In terms of cooking, the battery could easily handle my rice cooker and Instapot pressure cooker for extended cooking times. I was able to cook an 8 lb. pork roast in the pressure cooker. It also had enough power to run my air fryer and microwave. However, with the air fryer drawing as much as 1700 W, it depletes the capacity quickly, even though the load is within the 1800 W continuous rating of the battery. A kettle or coffee maker does not pose much of a challenge. You could also potentially run an electric grill, although I did not have the opportunity to try it yet. This could make a cookout more convenient, in addition to reducing risks associated with fire-based grills in dry areas.

After all that, I needed to clean up. I was able to run my dishwasher off the battery. Heating water is clearly one area that consumes a lot of energy, but I was able to run the dishwasher for a full cycle with room to spare. I was also able to run my portable washing machine off the battery. While the loads were not massive, the voltage fluctuates significantly while it is running. It did not create an issue for the battery. Of note, these are efficient NYC apartment-sized appliances. Many Europeans use similar-sized appliances, but middle-American McMansions tend to use more power-hungry models. Your mileage may vary.

It is 144 pages long, and you can read the entire report here . I will just be hitting the highlights and providing some comments along the way.
article_paragraphs: The Electric Vehicle Council has been tracking the progress of electric vehicle uptake in Australia over the last ten years. Their latest report is a celebration of achievements. It is 144 pages long, and you can read the entire report here . I will just be hitting the highlights and providing some comments along the way.

In a demonstration of how fast the EV transition is moving in Australia, the EVC report projections to the end of the year are already hopelessly out of date, with a surge over the last three months looking set to continue through to the end of the year. Nevertheless, the report makes encouraging reading.

Both BEV and PHEV sales have doubled comparing H1 2025 with H2 2026. A new EV is sold in Australia every 100 seconds as Australians seek to cut costs and gain energy security. The ratio of BEV to PHEV sits at 2:1, similar to many other countries. The report warns of a possible “fragility” in Australia’s EV sales due to increasing demand for public charging and the possible introduction of a road user charge.

The report says that so far installation of public charging has kept up with demand. This is due to the fact that most Australians charge at home. There are 4268 AC and DC public charging locations available, an increase of 18% year on year and 11,600 public AC and DC connectors, a 31% increase year on year.

Political threats might also derail the electric train of progress. Australia’s right wing political parties are threatening to remove the New Vehicle Efficiency Standards and the Fringe Benefit Tax exemption should they gain power. The battle is not yet won. Intense lobbying by vested interests in the auto industry (FCAI) has led to significant misrepresentation in the media. The FUD is ever with us.

The report notes that the FBT exemption has been reviewed and extended to 2029. This may be long enough for EVs to enter the second-hand market where most Australians buy their cars. Australia has set a target of 5 million BEVs on the road by 2035 — “uptake must keep accelerating” if the country is to achieve this target. At the time of this report’s publication, there were 612,000 BEVs on Australian roads.

The top 5 best-selling plugin EVs in the Australian market over the past 12 months have been: Tesla Model Y (20,400), BYD Sealion 7 (12,500), BYD Shark 6 PHEV (9,500), Geely EX 5 (6,800), and Jaecoo J5 (6,000). I don’t expect this to change as we rush towards the end of the year. CleanTechnica readers would have been familiar with this lineup from regular reports. For the latest one, see here.

A comparison with CleanTechnica ’s figures and those of the EVC will demonstrate how rapidly sales are increasing. YTD figures of each model listed in the CleanTechnica report are almost double that in the EVC report.

title: Verstappen collides with Lawson as Leclerc tops Mexico FP2
raw_summary: Charles Leclerc kept Ferrari on top in second practice for Formula 1’s 2026 Mexican Grand Prix, despite a messy session in which he twice went off the track and team-mate Lewis Hamilton broke down on track with an engine problem and Max Verstappen collided with Red Bull stablemate Liam Lawson. The Ferraris established a comfortable advantage during the early running on the harder Pirelli tyre compounds, despite a lurid slide through the esses from Leclerc, with him and Hamilton 1-2 using the medium tyre and six tenths clear of Oscar Piastri’s hard-tyred McLaren.
summary: Charles Leclerc kept Ferrari on top in second practice for Formula 1’s 2026 Mexican Grand Prix, despite a messy session in which he twice went off the track and team-mate Lewis Hamilton broke down on track with an engine problem and Max Verstappen collided with Red Bull stablemate Liam Lawson.
article_paragraphs: Charles Leclerc kept Ferrari on top in second practice for Formula 1’s 2026 Mexican Grand Prix, despite a messy session in which he twice went off the track and team-mate Lewis Hamilton broke down on track with an engine problem and Max Verstappen collided with Red Bull stablemate Liam Lawson.

The Ferraris established a comfortable advantage during the early running on the harder Pirelli tyre compounds, despite a lurid slide through the esses from Leclerc, with him and Hamilton 1-2 using the medium tyre and six tenths clear of Oscar Piastri’s hard-tyred McLaren.

Having sat out first practice, Verstappen decided to head straight out on the soft tyre but was only fifth fastest and a full second off the pace before a bizarre incident with Lawson that caused a red flag.
Verstappen dived inside the Racing Bulls on the brakes into Turn 12, gesticulating at Lawson as they exited the corner side by side.

Lawson remained on Verstappen’s inside through the following Turn 13 left-hand hairpin and the two then collided at the Turn 14 right-hander as Verstappen went off the track, over the inside kerb and into Lawson’s car.
The incident shattered the Red Bull’s left-hand-side bargeboard and a red flag stoppage was required to clear the debris.

Once the session resumed, championship leader Kimi Antonelli attempted a final run on the medium tyre that split the two Ferraris. He was absolutely level with Leclerc after two sectors, but encountered Pierre Gasly’s Alpine through the final sequence of turns and ended up three tenths off.

Leclerc maintained Ferrari’s place at the top of the timesheet in the qualifying simulations on soft tyres, despite running wide through Turn 12 after encountering Sergio Perez’s Cadillac on his first flying lap, then locking up heavily under braking for Turn 1 when he made a second attempt.

title: Mate Rimac Chased Down A Guy Who Stole His Bugatti Chiron In Croatia
raw_summary: For a Croatian man in his mid-30s, seeing a Bugatti Chiron sitting unattended with the keys inside was too hard to resist. The unnamed man stole the Chiron and fled across multiple countries, landing him in global headlines after Bugatti boss Mate Rimac revealed the man stole his very own Chiron. Earlier this week, Mate Rimac parked his dark blue Chiron at the Rimac Campus in Croatia with the key inside. Bugatti's CEO admits he always does this, as engineers are constantly driving and testing the car, so it's easier to just leave the key inside. As it turns out, the campus is completely open to the public, allowing one intrepid car thief to view this as an invitation to go for the joyride of a lifetime.

Security camera footage from the facility shows the hooded man scoping out the Chiron at the back of the Rimac campus. He finishes a cigarette, opens the driver's door, gets inside, and drives off casually. The Rimac team quickly discovered the car was missing, and Mate called the local police. Tracking data showed the Chiron's live location and that it was heading to Slovenia. Mate says he jumped in his Porsche 911 and gave chase.

The boss of Rimac Bugatti couldn't catch the thief as he sped through Slovenia and eventually entered Austria. There, police located the car and arrested him. Mate Rimac adds that as he headed to the same police station where the thief was being held to prove he owned the Chiron, he spoke to him. Bizarrely, the guy said he walked into the Rimac Campus looking for a job before noticing the Chiron was sitting there with the keys. Chances are, he probably thought he had struck gold and that this was the luckiest day of his life. He told Mate he hoped to drive the car to Germany, though it's unclear why.

Police in both Croatia and Austria are expected to file charges and prosecute the thief , given how expensive the car is. Incredibly, the car survived the theft with only a scuffed carbon-fiber front splitter, which the Bugatti team will need to repair. Mate has also learned a valuable lesson that despite how safe Croatia may be, it's never a good idea to leave a car unlocked with the keys inside.

raw_title: How We’d Spec It: 2027 BMW 3-Series
title: How We’d Spec It: 2027 BMW 3-Series
raw_summary: The BMW 3-series is the poster child for sports sedans, so it’s always exciting when a new generation debuts. The gas-powered Neue Klasse 3-series that can be configured on BMW’s consumer site is available with a 255-hp turbocharged 2.0 four-cylinder (330) or a 437-hp turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six (M350). In rear-wheel-drive form, the 330 starts at $51,250, while the all-wheel-drive-only M350 starts at $67,250. Regardless of powertrain, both Bimmers offer a wide selection of paint colors, wheel designs, and stand-alone options. That level of personalization makes the new 2027 BMW 3-series a perfect candidate for our How We’d Spec It series. I find BMW’s Neue Klasse era to be a bit overwhelming, so I kept things simple with my 3-series. Though the 437-hp six-cylinder M350 is tempting, the 255-hp four-cylinder 330 offers enough power for my needs, and I like that it’s available in a standard rear-wheel-drive configuration. Given that the new 3 is larger and heavier than ever, I’ll consider this to be the “superleggera” spec.

No timeframe has been given for a U.S. production launch.

Although still covered in camouflage in Honda's latest pictures, the HRC Civic clearly has a more aggressive front bumper, aerodynamic winglets over the front wheelarches, and a serious rear spoiler. Those tweaks all point to additional downforce, and we'd expect them to be paired with uprated springs and dampers, and larger brakes. The biggest question is whether HRC is able to liberate any more power from the turbocharged, 2.0L inline four. It currently makes 315 hp (319 PS) in U.S. trim, which is sent to the front wheels via a six-speed manual transmission.

The HRC is one solid reason to swing by Honda's SEMA stand next month (November 3-6, 2026), but it's not the only one. There's also Honda's Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck , which has a twin-turbo, 2.4L V6 powertrain that employs hybrid technology to help it wind out a monstrous 1,300+ horsepower (1,318 PS). The Trophy Truck is backed up by a trio of modified Passport Trailsport chase vehicles.

For anyone who's looked at the new Prelude hybrid coupe and wished Honda would junk the electric bits and drop in the Civic Type's engine and six-speed manual transmission, they'll want to check out the Hasport Prelude Club Racer. It's the modern-day Prelude most of us have dreamed about, but the Honda gurus at Arizona's Hasport wasn't content to leave the idea as a dream.

Felix Rosenqvist's 2026 Indy 500-winning Honda IndyCar, the Honda-powered 2026 Aston Martin Aramco Racing AMR26 F1 racer, and a 35-horsepower Honda N600 microcar that competed in the 1970 Baja 1000 race are also on display. And HRC U.S. is launching its line of official performance parts at SEMA 2026, including sports exhausts, lightweight forged wheels, and a short-throw shifter for models like the Civic Type R, Passport Trailsport and Integra Type S. Honda and Acura will offer the upgrades through dealerships and online starting March 2027.

raw_title: FAA Finally Certifies Boeing 737 Max 10 For Commercial Delivery, Bringing The Entire 737 Family Into Service
title: FAA Finally Certifies Boeing 737 Max 10 For Commercial Delivery, Bringing The Entire 737 Family Into Service
raw_summary: It has finally happened: the Federal Aviation Administration has certified the Boeing 737 Max 10, meaning that the entire range of the company's best-selling aircraft is now suitable for delivery to airlines in the U.S. The 10 variant is the largest of the 737 Max family, able to seat up to 210 passengers in a two-class configuration, making it something of a successor to the mid-size 757. It now joins its siblings, the 8 and 9 variants that have been flying for years, and the smallest 7 variant that only got certified a few months ago . This is great news for Boeing, which is on a hot streak lately: It recently recovered the ability to self-certify individual planes for safety and overtook archrival Airbus in annual sales . The 737 Max 10's certification was stuck on the runway for a long time before finally achieving liftoff. The variant flew its first test flight way back in 2021. This was after the horrible 737 Max crashes of 2018 and 2019, so the FAA was quite suspicious of the company and really put this model through the wringer. In addition, the Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act was passed in 2020, mandating much stricter standards. The 737 Max 10 is the first plane to go through the new process, though it took five years. You'll be pleased to learn that both Boeing and the FAA are aware of a software glitch that messes with the navigation system, but never mind that! The plane is flyable, and you might well be on one sometime next year.

It now joins its siblings, the 8 and 9 variants that have been flying for years, and the smallest 7 variant that only got certified a few months ago . This is great news for Boeing, which is on a hot streak lately: It recently recovered the ability to self-certify individual planes for safety and overtook archrival Airbus in annual sales .

The 737 Max 10's certification was stuck on the runway for a long time before finally achieving liftoff. The variant flew its first test flight way back in 2021. This was after the horrible 737 Max crashes of 2018 and 2019, so the FAA was quite suspicious of the company and really put this model through the wringer. In addition, the Aircraft Certification, Safety, and Accountability Act was passed in 2020, mandating much stricter standards. The 737 Max 10 is the first plane to go through the new process, though it took five years. You'll be pleased to learn that both Boeing and the FAA are aware of a software glitch that messes with the navigation system, but never mind that! The plane is flyable, and you might well be on one sometime next year.

Each of the 737 Max variants has its purpose. For the 10, being larger means that it can handle a route's passenger traffic in fewer flights, giving it the lowest per seat cost of any single-aisle aircraft, according to Boeing . Functionally, it's a replacement for the old 757, which the aviation sector has been waiting for a long time.

With a 3,100-nautical-mile range, the 10 can cover a broad range of routes; however, this is the shortest range of any 737 Max, which limits its appeal a bit. By contrast, the tiny 7 can go 3,800 nautical miles, which can cover the vast bulk of routes, though it can only carry up to 160 passengers in a two-class configuration. Still, the 7's light weight means it's great for high-altitude or high-temperature airports.

The all-around champions here are the 8 and its very close twin, the 9. You've probably been on one. The former can take up to 180 passengers up to 3,500 nautical miles; the latter can take up to 195 passengers up to 3,300 nautical miles. These two combined have made the 737 Max into Boeing's top seller ever. Getting the 7 and 10 certified adds icing to that cake.

It's a good amount of icing, though, since over 30% of current 737 Max orders are for the 10 variant. Simple Flying reports that Canadian airline WestJet will be the first to get the shiny new planes in early 2027 (provided that Canadian regulators also certify them). Boeing will then fulfill orders, all 1,555 of them, for other customers all over the world. Now all Boeing has to do is get the 777X finally certified .

title: Xpeng's G9L Lands As A Threat To The European Establishment
raw_summary: More Chinese EVs headed to Europe, but at least this one looks good It's not just BYD that has used the recent Paris Motor Show to unveil an important new SUV for the European market. Fellow Chinese brand Xpeng has done the same, unveiling its flagship G9L SUV in battery-electric and range-extender configurations. article_paragraphs: More Chinese EVs headed to Europe, but at least this one looks good

It's not just BYD that has used the recent Paris Motor Show to unveil an important new SUV for the European market. Fellow Chinese brand Xpeng has done the same, unveiling its flagship G9L SUV in battery-electric and range-extender configurations. If any European brands weren't taking the threat from China seriously, they now have to.

Xpeng has priced the G9L from €74,600 ($83,300) in Germany, and between €74,990 ($83,700) and €75,990 ($84,900) in other European markets, including France, Austria, and the Netherlands. This makes it comfortably cheaper than something like a new BMW X5, which starts at €102,800 ($114,800) in plug-in hybrid X5 50e xDrive configuration. The G9L won't only be sold in Europe either, as Xpeng plans to sell the G9L in 64 separate markets, including Australia and New Zealand. It's been designed as a truly global SUV and will be manufactured at the firm's plant in China and Magna Steyr's factory in Austria.

The range-extender version is perhaps the most intriguing. It uses a turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-four with a powerful electric motor and a 63-kWh lithium-ion phosphate battery, which itself is larger than the batteries of some smaller EVs. Xpeng says combined grunt sits at an impressive 577 horsepower and 513 pound-feet (695 Nm) of torque, allowing the EREV to hit 62 mph (100 km/h) in 5.4 seconds.

More impressive than the performance on offer is Xpeng's claim the G9L EREV can travel up to 270 miles (435 km) on electric power alone and has a combined driving range of 996 miles (1,602 km) on the optimistic CLTC cycle. The powertrain includes regenerative braking to maximize efficiency and intelligently adapts to the driving scenario. For example, if you're in an urban environment, it will prioritize electric power, and on a highway, the range-extender will be activated as required. Crucially, the engine never drives the wheels and only generates electricity, so the G9L EREV will accelerate as smoothly and instantly as a traditional EV.

Two all-electric versions have been announced alongside the EREV. Base models will use a 91.9-kWh battery while others will be available with a 110-kWh pack. The most powerful version will use a pair of electric motors with 577 hp and 513 lb-ft (695 Nm) of torque. This power does come at the cost of efficiency. On the WLTC cycle, the range of this version will be capped at 344 miles (553 km). Somewhat making up for that is that the G9L supports DC charging speeds of up to 540 kW, allowing the battery to be charged from 10 to 80% in under 12 minutes.

It's not just the available powertrains that may encourage some European buyers to ditch their BMWs and Audis for the Xpeng G9L. It is rocks the company's latest intelligent driving technologies that include city and highway assisted driving, navigation-based assisted driving, and intelligent hands-free lane changes.

The G9L's cabin also prioritizes luxury and comfort. Found in the front row are Nappa leather seats with heating, ventilation, and a 16-point massage function. The second row will be available with either a bench seat or captain's chairs, all trimmed in the same Nappa leather as the front and also include heating, ventilation, and massage functions. As for the third row, it includes heated seats and a 50:50 split folding function.

raw_title: Rivian R2 Sales Are So Strong It’s Outselling Both R1 Models Combined
title: Rivian R2 Sales Are So Strong It’s Outselling Both R1 Models Combined
raw_summary: The cat’s out of the bag. The Rivian R2 is good, and customers know it. In fact, they’re so in the know that the R2 is outselling the R1T and R1S combined, the company confirmed during its third-quarter earnings call. Along with outselling the other customer-focused products, the R2 is also outselling Rivian’s EDV delivery vans. Those strong sales figures come in spite of Rivian still selling the R2 in just its most expensive Performance trim, which starts at $59,485. The $55,485 Premium trim and the long-awaited $46,485 base model are still MIA, with no clear arrival date scheduled. Rivian’s consumer site currently lists the R2 Premium as arriving in late 2026, while the Standard isn’t set to arrive until some time next year. Even in its most expensive form, the R2 is considerably less expensive than its pickup- and three-row SUV stablemates, which start at $81,885 and $85,885, respectively.

Mercedes’ Vesti was the fastest rookie in FP1, with every team bar Ferrari fielding a substitute for FP1.
Leclerc’s team-mate Lewis Hamilton was 0.005s off Vesti in fourth, the top four having set their fastest times on softs.
Red Bull stand-in Ayumu Iwasa meanwhile went fifth, 0.985s off the pace, on mediums.
Pierre Gasly took sixth for Alpine, just over a second away, while his rookie team-mate Gabriele Mini was 14th.

title: Mate Rimac Chased His Stolen Bugatti Chiron Across The Border In His 911 After It Was Nabbed From Rimac HQ
raw_summary: As the CEO of Bugatti Rimac responsible for making some of the most powerful and fastest interal-combustion and electrified vehicles in the world, Mate Rimac was already a pretty cool dude, but the latest situation he found himself in takes things to another level. Rimac, being the very rich and apparently very trusting man that he is, decided it's a good idea to leave his cars unlocked with the keys inside them at his company's headquarters in Croatia, in case employees ever needed to move them. It hadn't really been an issue for the 38-year-old ... until now. Rimac, as he always does, left his Bugatti Chiron unlocked with the keys in it outside a garage at the company's campus recently when everything went very wrong. An employee spotted the seven-figure supercar speeding away and quickly alerted colleagues, according to an Instagram video posted by the CEO. A group of employees quickly figured out that no one authorized the vehicle to be moved, and somebody had indeed stolen the car. Rimac didn't take this news lying down. Of course, he contacted police, but he also jumped behind the wheel of his fully fueled Porsche 911 (we think it's this very nice purple 992.2 Turbo S that coincidentally uses Rimac batteries) and went after the stolen car at "full throttle."

article_paragraphs: As the CEO of Bugatti Rimac responsible for making some of the most powerful and fastest interal-combustion and electrified vehicles in the world, Mate Rimac was already a pretty cool dude, but the latest situation he found himself in takes things to another level. Rimac, being the very rich and apparently very trusting man that he is, decided it's a good idea to leave his cars unlocked with the keys inside them at his company's headquarters in Croatia, in case employees ever needed to move them. It hadn't really been an issue for the 38-year-old ... until now.

Rimac, as he always does, left his Bugatti Chiron unlocked with the keys in it outside a garage at the company's campus recently when everything went very wrong. An employee spotted the seven-figure supercar speeding away and quickly alerted colleagues, according to an Instagram video posted by the CEO. A group of employees quickly figured out that no one authorized the vehicle to be moved, and somebody had indeed stolen the car. Rimac didn't take this news lying down. Of course, he contacted police, but he also jumped behind the wheel of his fully fueled Porsche 911 (we think it's this very nice purple 992.2 Turbo S that coincidentally uses Rimac batteries) and went after the stolen car at "full throttle."

Luckily for Rimac, the Bugatti was equipped with live telemetry, meaning that, despite the thief having a one-hour head start, he and his colleagues were able to tell exactly where the car was and relay that information back to Croatian police.

There was hope that police would intercept the Chiron and the thief before it left Croatia, but that wasn't meant to be. In fact, it made it all the way to Austria, crossing through Slovenia in the process. In Austria, the driver found himself low on fuel — not a terrible surprise given the Chiron has a quad-turbo W16 engine . After throwing half a tank of fuel in the car, which he didn't pay for, he continued driving. Eventually, Austrian police were able to catch up with him thanks to information from Rimac's group chat.

Rimac says he had decided not to press charges against the man who stole his car, but that doesn't mean he's going to walk away scot-free. I'm sure the police in Croatia, Austria, and possibly Slovenia are going to want to talk to him. Initially, Rimac, maybe with a bit of naivety, thought he'd be able to just pick up the car from the cops and drive the thief back home to his family, no harm, no foul, but "because of the value of the car, there was like 10 police cars," and he couldn't just take the car back. However, just a day later he got it back after proving he was the real owner. Apparently, the thief was local to Croatia, and had shown up to the Rimac HQ asking for job before he stole the Chiron.

The incident has already changed Rimac's approach to locking his cars' doors. He's no longer going to leave keys lying around or leave cars unlocked. At the beginning of his video, he says Croatia is "super, super safe," which he admits might sound strange to folks in the U.S. and abroad. That's why he always felt fine leaving his cars unlocked.
"I did that for years, and nothing ever happened. Until, of course, something did happened, so I will not do that anymore," Rimac joked on Instagram . "Don't try your luck — will not happen again."

raw_summary: One of the best concept cars of this year was the Vision BMW Alpina , a stunning two-door coupe that previews the direction the Alpina brand is going now that it's fully under BMW's control. BMW recently showed off the M760, which has a twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8 making around 570 horsepower, and the B7 should share that same powertrain just with even more power — the last B7 had 600 hp . The Vision concept had a real V8 in it that made very good noises from its lovely quad exhaust, and this B7 prototype has the same exhaust, which is a good sign.
I don't need that as a sign to know it sounds good, though. These spy shots were taken at the Nürburgring, and as you can hear from the clip above, this B7 prototype sounds quite good itself.

In addition to the quad exhaust, this prototype has a unique front grille with horizontal lower slats, a larger and wider lower bumper intake, and a prominent chin splitter, an Alpina hallmark. There's a little spoiler on the trunk lid, and the rear diffuser is new. New BMW M cars like the M350 and iX4 M60 feature yellow LED running lights, and it seems like the Alpina models will have a different amber shade, like the Vision concept. The big wheels are a design we haven't seen before, but I don't think they'll be the final ones. BMW has already said Alpina will stick with its classic multispoke designs.

Expect the B7 to get its own suspension and chassis tuning that give it a more comfortable, grown-up vibe compared to M cars, focused on grand touring performance. There will surely be Alpina-specific paint colors (the brand is known for its emerald greens and sapphire blues) and exterior graphics packages, while the interior will have crystal controls, Alpina's signature blue and green stitching and other patterns, special badging and other touches.

It shouldn't be long before the new Alpina B7 gets revealed and goes on sale, and it will be closely followed (or maybe even preceded) by the Alpina XB7 version of the next-gen X7 that recently got spotted .

title: Fuel From Bamboo Costs Just $2.75 Per Gallon
raw_summary: At CleanTechnica , we are passionate champions of the “electrify everything” movement promoted by Tony Seba and Mark Jacobson, among others. However, being realistic, internal combustion engines will continue to play an important role in transportation by land, sea, and air for the remainder of this century and perhaps beyond. Almost any plant that grows could potentially be turned into a biofuel with a lower emissions footprint than gasoline or diesel. Currently in the US, millions of tons of corn are used every year to make ethanol , which is then blended with gasoline. In theory, the ethanol helps lower emissions, but the reduction, if any, is modest and it decreases fuel economy, so motorist are actually using more fuel than they would if they used ordinary, unadulterated gasoline.

article_paragraphs: At CleanTechnica , we are passionate champions of the “electrify everything” movement promoted by Tony Seba and Mark Jacobson, among others. However, being realistic, internal combustion engines will continue to play an important role in transportation by land, sea, and air for the remainder of this century and perhaps beyond.

Almost any plant that grows could potentially be turned into a biofuel with a lower emissions footprint than gasoline or diesel. Currently in the US, millions of tons of corn are used every year to make ethanol , which is then blended with gasoline. In theory, the ethanol helps lower emissions, but the reduction, if any, is modest and it decreases fuel economy, so motorist are actually using more fuel than they would if they used ordinary, unadulterated gasoline.

The other part of the equation is that the conversion process itself requires a fair amount of energy and makes its own greenhouse gas emissions, which politicians conveniently choose to ignore. Ethanol , then, is mostly a scam that rewards farmers, but has few other benefits. While the science is sound, the rewards are far less than claimed. However, farmers are an important political group and no one wants to tell them that corn for ethanol is no longer a thing.

Researchers at Worcester Polytechnic Institute think they have found a better way. In a study published September 24, 2026 in the Royal Society of Chemistry journal Sustainable Energy And Fuels , Michael Timko, the head of the chemical engineering department at WPI, and Timothy Woodard, PhD, claim that bamboo may be the perfect source material for making biofuels. In the published study, they write:

“Corn stover, an agricultural residue widely available in the U.S., has been one of the most studied biomass sources for biofuel production.6 Yet its relatively modest yields and high ash content have created significant challenges for scaling up production. Alternative feedstocks such as switch grass have been explored, but these offer only incremental improvements in performance relative to corn stover, particularly in ash content and growth rate. These limitations highlight the importance of identifying and evaluating less conventional biomass sources that may offer superior attributes for fuel production.

“Bamboo has emerged as a strong candidate due to its rapid growth, high productivity per unit area, and low input requirements. Some bamboo species reach their full height within a few months and mature within four years. Bamboo’s deep root systems improve soil stability, promote subsurface carbon sequestration, and support water conservation. It can also be grown on marginal or degraded land, reducing competition with food crops and offering economic opportunities for rural communities.

“Critically, bamboo also possesses an exceptionally low ash content compared with most lignocellulosic feedstocks, which minimizes inorganic fouling and catalyst poisoning during thermochemical conversion and improves the quality of the resulting biocrude. Furthermore, the presence of ash complicates thermochemical conversion to products, with frequently reported adverse effects on yields.

“The characteristics of fast growth, low fertilizer and water use, and low ash content make bamboo stand out as a promising source of biomass that can achieve economic competitiveness that has not been obtained with other feedstocks. Unfortunately, despite these advantages, bamboo remains largely underexplored as a feedstock for liquid fuel production, especially in thermochemical conversion processes such as hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL).”

Dakar Rally organizers let fans use their imaginations as to why the event was temporarily moved out of Saudi Arabia, using the vague explanation, "In light of recent events." But it's not hard to connect the dots and realize it was due to the U.S. war against Iran.

While the war has cooled in recent months , Saudi Arabia became the direct target of a renewed offensive by Houthi forces in Yemen amid their ongoing conflict. Earlier this month, the Houthis launched a barrage of drones and missiles at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and two other international airports. The attacks killed at least 21 people and injured over 300 more. Also, U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly implied that the United States would resume hostilities against Iran after next week's midterm elections. It simply wasn't safe to run the Dakar Rally anywhere in the region.

The Dakar Rally is no stranger to relocation. As the event name implies, it was originally a cross-country rally from Paris to Dakar in Senegal . It largely remained that way from 1979 until 2008, when four French tourists were killed by a North African wing of al-Qaida and the race was canceled. Fearing that the Dakar could be a target for insurgents in the Maghreb, the rally relocated to South America from 2009 until 2019. The Amaury Sport Organization, Dakar's organizers, moved the event to Saudi Arabia in 2020 after signing a multi-year deal with the country . The return to Africa in 2027 will only be temporary because of how lucrative the Saudi agreement must be.

title: Tesla drops car referral rewards, now pays owners in FSD for referrals
raw_summary: Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying. At the same time, Tesla’s Refer and Earn terms no longer list any vehicle as a qualifying purchase for buyer or referrer rewards. Buy a Tesla with a friend’s code today and neither of you gets anything.
summary: Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying.
article_paragraphs: Tesla has launched a new referral program in the US that pays owners in Full Self-Driving (Supervised) instead of rewarding car sales. A referred owner gets one free month of FSD, and the referrer gets a free month or a $99 Tesla Credit if that person starts paying.

At the same time, Tesla’s Refer and Earn terms no longer list any vehicle as a qualifying purchase for buyer or referrer rewards. Buy a Tesla with a friend’s code today and neither of you gets anything.

To share a link, you need to be paying for FSD (Supervised) monthly or own it outright from before Tesla stopped selling it, according to Tesla’s FSD referral support page . Owners who got FSD through a one-year grant can’t participate. The link lives under “Refer and Earn” in the Tesla app, version 4.62.0 or later.

The person on the other end has to own a registered Tesla with compatible hardware, can’t have paid for FSD in the past 12 months, and can’t have bought it outright. There’s also a catch for recent buyers: anyone who got a free FSD trial with a new car is locked out of referral links until 12 months after that trial ends.

If the friend converts, subscribers get a free month and outright owners get a $99 credit, the same as one month of the subscription. Credits expire after 12 months and can’t be cashed out. Tesla caps it at 12 rewards per calendar year, so the most anyone can earn is a year of FSD or $1,188 in credits.
Tesla’s own pages don’t quite agree on timing. The FSD page says the referrer is rewarded when the friend subscribes during the trial, while the main Refer and Earn page says after it.

The bigger change is buried in Tesla’s Refer and Earn page . Buyer benefits now apply to solar panels only. Referrer benefits cover solar, first demo drives (up to 30 over an account’s lifetime) and the new FSD referral.
Model 3, Model Y and Cybertruck only show up under loyalty benefits, for existing owners buying another Tesla product. Model S and Model X aren’t listed at all.

title: Polaris Has Just Created A Dune Buggy With More Power Than An Audi RS3

article_paragraphs: Polaris put sports car power into its sand-slinging buggy, which debuts at the 2027 King of the Hammers desert race

A couple of months ago, Polaris unveiled an extreme version of its popular RZR , badged the Pro R Boost. With a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four and 275 horsepower, it's a side-by-side that packs a serious punch. Polaris obviously wasn't satisfied with Hyundai Elantra N levels of performance and has now unveiled an even crazier version of the RZR with significantly more grunt. Meet the RZR Pro R Factory Boost.

Unlike the standard Pro R Boost, the Pro R Factory Boost is designed for desert and sand racing. It uses a new turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder known as the ProStar Fury with 400 hp. We don't yet know how much torque this engine has, though with 400 hp, the latest RZR has more power than a U.S.-spec Audi RS3 with 394 hp. That should make it an absolute weapon in the sand and on pretty much any other terrain imaginable.

The RZR Pro R Factory Boost is so focused that it features lightweight carbon fiber bodywork and has been designed to slice through the air at over 100 mph. This explains why it looks much sleeker than the normal, consumer-focused RZR Pro R. It also benefits from a 6.5-inch longer wheelbase to improve stability and body control. A set of beefy BF Goodrich tires connects the side-by-side to the terrain, while custom three-inch internal bypass Dynamix DV Live Valve shocks soak up any and all bumps. A Fox steering damper absorbs larger impacts.

The modifications don't stop here. The RZR Pro R Factory Boost includes a new competition-ready cage and a cab that's two inches wider. It also includes a large 34-gallon fuel tank and has a driving range of more than 200 miles. A full MoTeC package and ECU with different power distribution settings control the 2.0-liter engine's monstrous power output.

Each example will be built by the Polaris RZR Factory Racing team, and the RZR Pro R Factory Boost will make its competitive debut at the 2027 King of The Hammers event running from January 21, 2027, through to February 6, 2027. Crucially, you don't need to run a racing team or be a competitive racer to buy one, but you will need a lot of money. Prices start at $200,000, or almost three times the starting price of the aforementioned Audi RS3. Evidently, you'll need to be a serious off-roading enthusiast to drop this kind of money on a non-road-legal side-by-side.

Although it already sells Woodland versions of the RAV4, Sienna, bZ, and most recently, the Grand Highlander, Toyota said the new family of concept vehicles is “designed for drivers who see adventure not as a destination, but a way of life.”
Toyota’s North American design studio, CALTY Design Research, designed the concepts to explore how some of its most popular nameplates can be used better on and off the road.
Each vehicle features Horizon Blue exterior paint, inspired by Toyota’s 1960s models, including the Stout, Crown, and Corona.

All new concepts also include an exclusive Woodland badge, plus a lift kit, large over-fenders, satin-black wheels, All-Terrain tires, two-tone paint on the roof and hood, a roof rack, and cross bars to top it off.
According to Toyota, the RAV4 Woodland Plug-In Hybrid and Sienna Woodland Concepts show how its “electrified and family-focused vehicles take on a more adventurous role.”

The electric Woodland bZ Concept “extends the Woodland theme into Toyota’s battery electric future.” Meanwhile, the Grand Highlander Woodland Concept and Crown Signia Woodland Concept bring two distinct models to the lineup, Toyota said.

title: Koenigsegg's Latest $3.6 Million Hypercar Has Just Been Recalled
raw_summary: No matter how expensive a new car may be, there's a good chance it'll be recalled at some stage. For the Koenigsegg CC850 , that time has come, and now all seven examples delivered in the United States need to be fixed because of an issue with the electronic parking brake. The NHTSA says Koenigsegg received a report of a CC850 rolling away in the U.S. on October 12. According to the recall notice, the driver exited the vehicle with the engine running and reverse gear engaged, causing it to start rolling away. The notice doesn't say whether any damage occurred, though the incident prompted the Swedish hypercar manufacturer to launch an investigation. After a week of internal testing, Koenigsegg discovered that the parking brake will not engage while the transmission is in Reverse and the engine is running. In this case, the only way to engage the parking brake is to hold the button down continuously. The NHTSA says this condition falls outside the scope of its static parking brake tests, so it appears Koenigsegg issued this recall of its own accord, not because the CC850 fails to comply with any Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards.

Koenigsegg manufactured the seven impacted vehicles between September 28, 2025 and August 2, 2026. All of these CC850s will receive a free over-the-air software update to resolve the issue. If customers opt against having the software update implemented, they'll have the opportunity to bring their vehicle to an authorized Koenigsegg dealership and have the update completed on site.

The CC850 stands out from other Koenigsegg models in part by using the Swedish automaker's part-manual, part-auto nine-speed Lightspeed transmission . It uses three shafts and seven clutches, and can be operated with a traditional clutch pedal as well as a gated manual transmission. Alternatively, the CC850 can be driven like a typical automatic. Ferrari recently introduced its own manual transmission for the 12Cilindri , which has a similar philosophy to Koenigsegg's approach. However, the Ferrari version operates as an add-on to the existing dual-clutch transmission.

title: It Didn't Take Long For Someone To Make The New Audi RS 5 Even Crazier
raw_summary: For those who thought the Audi RS 5 wasn't hot enough, ABT created a 710-hp version of both the Sedan and Avant Audi has a serious rival for the BMW M3 Touring in the new-generation RS5 Avant , pairing raw power with a sensational design. summary: For those who thought the Audi RS 5 wasn't hot enough, ABT created a 710-hp version of both the Sedan and Avant Audi has a serious rival for the BMW M3 Touring in the new-generation RS5 Avant , pairing raw power with a sensational design.
article_paragraphs: For those who thought the Audi RS 5 wasn't hot enough, ABT created a 710-hp version of both the Sedan and Avant

Audi has a serious rival for the BMW M3 Touring in the new-generation RS5 Avant , pairing raw power with a sensational design. It serves as the perfect antidote to all the boring EVs flooding the market. Now, German tuner and race team ABT Sportsline is developing an upgraded version of the RS5, giving it more power than even the limited-edition Audi RS6 GT .

ABT's creation, the RS5-R, follows a similar formula to other upgrade packages the firm sells. The firm started by looking at how it could make this beast even more intoxicating. To do this, they tweaked the software for the twin-turbocharged 2.9-liter V6 and the electric motor, resulting in a combined 710 horsepower and 667 pound-feet (905 Nm) of torque. The 80 hp and 59 lb-ft (80 Nm) gains should transform how this beast drives and let it easily outperform an RS6, even though that car has two extra cylinders. This is just the start of what ABT is developing for the RS5. Next year, it will release another performance upgrade with an Akrapovic titanium exhaust, helping the engine churn out 789 hp.

The upgrades extend beyond the engine. ABT has designed an eye-catching aerodynamic kit for the RS5-R with a sharp new front splitter, louvers on the front wheel arches, extended side skirts, and new wing mirrors. Stretching out from the roof is a large spoiler, and working with it to stick the rear wheels to the pavement is a striking rear diffuser. These parts are available in either standard carbon fiber or forged carbon fiber.

Oftentimes, the wheels of a modified car can make or break the overall design. In the case of the RS5-R, ABT has designed new 22-inch forged wheels with a gloss black finish and bold triangular spokes, clad in huge 315/25 tires. A set of lowering springs adds to the car's overall road presence, while sportier anti-roll bars have also been fitted.

ABT plans to sell just 130 examples of its RS5-R package, and each will include a special numbered plaque in the cabin. Speaking of the cabin, it will also include newly trimmed seats, an even plusher dashboard, and red contrast stitching. Carbon fiber paddle shifters complete the modifications.

For as impressive as all of the upgrades are, they're not cheap. In fact, prices for the RS5-R package start at €62,000 ($69,400) for the Sedan and Avant and €65,000 ($72,800) for the Avant when equipped with a standard carbon fiber finish, or an extra €3,000 ($3,300) for forged carbon fiber. ABT also charges a hefty €7,160 ($8,000) installation fee for the Sedan and €7,600 ($8,500) for the Avant. Oh, and all of these prices are in addition to the price of the actual car, which starts at €106,200 for the Sedan and €107,850 for the Avant (U.S. pricing and availability have yet to be announced).

title: A British Marque Is Building a New Audi Quattro with a 10,000-RPM V-8
raw_summary: Few cars have as famed a history as the Audi Quattro, and even fewer cars have been reimagined as many times. The newest tribute to Audi’s legendary Quattro is the Audacious Automotive IV. It’s being built by a small British manufacturer whose passion drove it to fit its creation with a V-8 that revs to 10,000 rpm. The IV combines B7-generation Audi RS4 underpinnings with the look—and in some cases, bodywork—of the short-wheelbase Audi Quattro. While the Quattro was famous for its five-cylinder engine, Audacious felt the RS4’s 4.2-liter V-8 was a better fit for its tribute car.

Coincidentally enough, the builder says the IV will be offered with four engine configurations. The standard setup takes the 4.2-liter V-8 and adds a supercharger, increasing power to 592 ponies. Strengthened internals and improved cooling from Audacious’ Stage Two conversion bring that figure to 740 hp. Plus, there are supercharged and naturally aspirated options that raise the engine’s redline from an already lofty 8250 to an otherworldly 10,000 rpm. It doesn’t seem like the higher redline offers any additional power, but it should sound the business.

raw_title: Electric Hydrofoils Save Energy, But Do They Earn Their Price?
title: Electric Hydrofoils Save Energy, But Do They Earn Their Price?
raw_summary: Hydrofoils have an obvious appeal. Lift a boat’s hull clear of the water, reduce drag and move passengers faster while consuming less energy. I’ve written before about the proposed electric hydrofoil ferry between Vancouver, Bowen Island and Gibsons, where floating logs, coastal conditions and uncertain passenger demand make the economics difficult. Hydrofoils have been commercially available for decades, but their operating niche remains narrower than their technical appeal suggests. A different opportunity emerged when Antwerp pilotage operator Brabo ordered an Artemis EF-12 electric hydrofoil pilot boat in August 2024. The vessel combines electric propulsion with submerged foils and active controls. Artemis has also demonstrated ship-contact manoeuvres using its EF-12 workboat platform, while the EF-12 Pilot design entered sea trials in 2026. The handling benefits are relevant to pilot transfers even when the boat isn’t operating at full speed.

article_paragraphs: Hydrofoils have an obvious appeal. Lift a boat’s hull clear of the water, reduce drag and move passengers faster while consuming less energy. I’ve written before about the proposed electric hydrofoil ferry between Vancouver, Bowen Island and Gibsons, where floating logs, coastal conditions and uncertain passenger demand make the economics difficult. Hydrofoils have been commercially available for decades, but their operating niche remains narrower than their technical appeal suggests.

A different opportunity emerged when Antwerp pilotage operator Brabo ordered an Artemis EF-12 electric hydrofoil pilot boat in August 2024. The vessel combines electric propulsion with submerged foils and active controls. Artemis has also demonstrated ship-contact manoeuvres using its EF-12 workboat platform, while the EF-12 Pilot design entered sea trials in 2026. The handling benefits are relevant to pilot transfers even when the boat isn’t operating at full speed.

The financial question is whether a hydrofoil can spend enough of its working life taking advantage of its design. Antwerp pilot boats work around locks, docks, ship movements and changing assignments. Reaching a high maximum speed is of limited value when the vessel spends much of its day manoeuvring or travelling through constrained waterways.

I tested that question using a Python-based operating model with synthetic assignments and three hypothetical sets of port-speed permissions. Depending on how much suitable high-speed water was available, the EF-12 spent zero, approximately 6% or approximately 13% of its underway time foilborne. These are modeled scenarios, not measurements of Brabo’s operations or actual Antwerp speed authorizations.

The resulting financial comparison was unflattering to the hydrofoil. In the central case, the EF-12’s modeled fifteen-year discounted cost was approximately €5.32 million, compared with €3.81 million for a conventional diesel tender, a premium of about 40%. Both figures include purchasing new vessels, rather than comparing a new hydrofoil with the marginal cost of keeping an existing diesel boat.

Electric propulsion still brought substantial energy benefits. The hydrofoil’s problem was that lower purchased energy did not compensate for the assumed capital cost and the limited opportunity to operate in its most efficient regime. Its active controls and potential ride-quality benefits remain relevant, but the available evidence did not justify assigning them a financial value.

An alternative electric approach also deserves consideration. Norway’s Moen Marin and Pascal Technologies have developed an air-cavity electric personnel vessel that reduces hull resistance without lifting most of the vessel above the water. It performed better financially than the hydrofoil in the exploratory comparison, although the existing craft was designed for aquaculture work and would require appropriate adaptation and certification before serving as a pilot tender.

The lesson resembles the one I drew from the Vancouver hydrofoil ferry proposal . Hydrofoils can be excellent machines, especially where sustained high-speed passages and suitable sea conditions allow them to exploit their advantages. In congested harbours, their additional complexity and capital cost need much stronger justification.

article_paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton intends to continue racing in Formula 1 “for the foreseeable future” if he can remain competitive, having been asked if he can realistically expect to race in the newly-announced African Grand Prix.
Earlier this month F1 revealed its plan for a new race in Rwanda, which will hold the title of the African GP, from 2030 at the earliest.
Hamilton, a long-standing figure who pushed for F1 to return to Africa, would therefore need to remain in the series well into his 40s to compete in the inaugural race in Rwanda.

The 41-year-old dismissed doubts he would retire from F1 before the first African GP would take place despite acknowledging he would be in his mid-40s if the race was to take place in 2030 – the earliest the event is planned, subject to track and infrastructure construction being completed in that time frame.
“Firstly, you've never had anyone like me here in the 70 years. I feel that I'm built differently,” Hamilton said ahead of this weekend’s Mexican GP.

“Of course, there are challenges up ahead that I can't foresee, that come with age. But along this way, along this journey, there have been so many preconceived ideas about the fact that your reaction time drops off. Did you see my reaction in the last race? My reaction is faster than some of the youngest people here.

“So there are lots of tools that you can utilise to continue to keep yourself, your mind sharp, as long as you're willing to sacrifice everything, which I am right now. I can't say in four years whether I want to continue to do what I'm doing, but I love what I'm doing still now.
“I'm still all in, and I will be for the foreseeable future.

article_paragraphs: Earlier this month, McLaren told the world that the 750S supercar will end production sometime next year. Naturally, we wondered what will come next. While there’s still a lot we have to learn, McLaren today confirmed the name of the successor to the 750S as well as its horsepower rating.

The McL 820 will be McLaren’s next supercar. The name was initially teased on a giant kiwi statue (pictured below) that the automaker unveiled in central London, with its body wearing a camouflage wrap featuring the “McL 820” name. For anyone who is confused about why McLaren chose a flightless bird endemic to New Zealand as its mascot, the company’s founder, Bruce McLaren, is from that country and originally used the kiwi as a visual centerpiece for his racing team’s branding.

Like with McLaren’s previous model names, the numeric designation represents their output in metric horsepower (a.k.a. PS). That continues with the McL 820, with 820 PS converting to 809 mechanical horsepower. That’s a considerable uptick versus its predecessor, with the standard 750S making 740 horses. The “McL” prefix is also new for the company’s production cars, though it was previewed on the McL 6GT that was revealed during this year’s Monterey Car Week. McLaren says its next supercar will mark the start of a new naming convention that incorporates McL.

There’s obviously still a lot of mystery surrounding the forthcoming McL 820, but McLaren says that information will start to be revealed next year, with the car itself also slated to hit the streets and racetracks sometime in 2027.

title: Even The Electric Golf Couldn't Survive VW's Financial Meltdown
raw_summary: VW Group has officially confirmed that development of the electric ninth-generation Golf has been delayed indefinitely due to the financial hardships within the company. The announcement was part of Wolfsburg's results for the period January-September 2026, painting a difficult picture for the German automaker that is especially unfortunate given Europe's COTY shortlist is an EV clean sweep . David Powels, Chief Financial Officer of the Volkswagen brand and Brand Group Core, said, "The market environment remains extremely challenging — and special items are weighing on our result. This makes it all the more important for us to systematically continue on our chosen course and sharpen our priorities further...One specific measure is therefore to temporarily pause development work on the future ID.Golf at the Volkswagen brand until we can securely accommodate the necessary investments".
