David Powels, Chief Financial Officer of the Volkswagen brand and Brand Group Core, said, "The market environment remains extremely challenging — and special items are weighing on our result. This makes it all the more important for us to systematically continue on our chosen course and sharpen our priorities further...One specific measure is therefore to temporarily pause development work on the future ID.Golf at the Volkswagen brand until we can securely accommodate the necessary investments".

The CFO said he is happy with the sales performance of their current EV lineup, but he is also worried about tightening profit margins. "Our electric vehicles are attractive, and we are seeing a significant upturn in demand. At the same time, they do not yet achieve the margins of our combustion engine models — this means the rising share of BEVs is currently increasing cost pressure. We are therefore systematically working on product costs, economies of scale, and a competitive cost base to achieve the necessary profitability for our electric models as well."

Development of the fully electric Golf hasn't been running smoothly. Initially planned to launch in 2028, the rollout of the compact hatchback was pushed back due to software glitches and brand prioritization for the new Scalable Systems Platform (SSP) architecture. Following the latest delay, the ID.Golf could hit the roads sometime in the 2030s. This means that the current ICE-powered eighth-generation Golf will likely stick around for over a decade, as it was introduced in late 2019 and received a mid-lifecycle update in early 2024.

The same applies to the electric ID.3 which entered production in 2019, benefited from mild updates in 2023 and from a more extensive facelift in 2026 when it adopted the ID.3 Neo badge . Based on the timeline, VW will likely consider introducing more styling and tech updates for both the Golf and the ID.3 Neo, in order to keep them relevant against newer competitors. Still, the hatchbacks will retain the existing MQB Evo and MEB underpinnings, leaving the most important changes for their SSP-based successor utilizing a new software architecture co-developed with Rivian.

Of course, the ID.Golf is not the only casualty of the financial crisis within the company. The VW Group lineup will be halved over the next few years, and the workforce will be further reduced by up to 50,000 people totaling around 100,000 lay offs since 2024. As for VW Group's results for the first nine months of 2026, they were mostly negative compared to the same period in 2025.

More specifically, net cash flow plummeted by 67% to €1.434 billion ($1.60 billion), operating result dropped by 8.3% to €4.326 billion ($4.825 billion), and revenue dropped by 0.5% to €106.417 billion ($118.67). Finally, sales were reduced 0.5% to 3,753,000 vehicles, and the operating margin fell from 4.4% last year to 4.1%. Out of the separate brands of the group, VW Passenger Cars was hit hard with 1.8% fewer sales, 3% less sales revenue, a 45% worse operating result, and a 44% drop to its operating margin.

article_paragraphs: Only 30 examples of the X-Bow XA will be sold in the U.S., and prices are expected to start just under $500,000

For almost 20 years, the KTM X-Bow has been unavailable in the U.S. market. The forthcoming introduction of the new X-Bow GT-XA will change that. This limited-edition, road-legal version of the X-Bow is being federalized for local use by KTM partner Carbon Yard and will provide wealthy Americans with one of the most hardcore driving experiences available.

The X-Bow GT-XA is very similar to the GT-XR that's been sold in Europe for several years. Unlike the original X-Bow , the GT-XR and GT-XA have a full windshield and a canopy-style roof, making them slightly more usable on the road. KTM will manufacture just 30 examples of the American-bound GT-XA, with prices expected to start at around $490,000. If the car is swiftly approved for sale in the U.S., customer deliveries should start next year. Orders are now open and require a $50,000 deposit.

The GT-XA is expected to largely mimic the GT-XR , which itself has been upgraded for 2027 with the new Factory 600 package. This model uses Audi's familiar turbocharged 2.5-liter five-cylinder, with a new turbo, intake manifold, and larger intercooler, delivering 592 horsepower. It pairs this sonorous engine with a dual-clutch transmission and a mechanical limited-slip differential driving the rear wheels.

KTM says American models will have several unique touches. These include a new suspension system with adjustable compression and rebound, plus a front-axle lift system. The GT-XA will also offer tire-pressure monitoring, and customers can choose custom materials, colors, trim, and interior stitching. According to the Austrian firm, the GT-XA aims to combine the X-Bow's brilliant track capabilities with extra composure and comfort for the street.

KTM will build each car meticulously by hand at its facility, and owners can spend time with engineers and attend exclusive driving experiences, including at the Red Bull Ring. KTM's exclusive U.S. partner Carbon Yard is handling local operations and will sell the GT-XA through select partners.

Like the European-spec GT-XR , America's GT-XA is built around a lightweight carbon fiber monocoque and is based heavily on the GTX and GT2 race cars that KTM builds. The visual highlight of the car is the jet-fighter-inspired canopy, which lifts up from the bodywork, bringing with it the carbon fiber roof, windshield, and the side windows. Much like a proper race car, the GT-XA will also come standard with fixed seats and uses an adjustable pedal box and steering wheel so owners can find their perfect driving position.

KTM famously fell on hard times in 2024 and went into self-administration while struggling with hundreds of millions of euros worth of debt. The motorcycle arm of the firm was sold to Indian manufacturer Bajaj Auto, and the company behind the X-Bow has been split off into a separate company. It is now being backed by a Belgian investment consortium that includes racing driver Guillaume de Mévius.

By now, everyone knows that EV sales cratered last fall, after US President Donald Trump and his Republican majority in Congress engineered the “OBBA” tax bill to eliminate federal tax credits for EVs.

Still, EV sales did not actually stop in their tracks, let alone reverse course. A fresh wave of off-lease, used EVs helped keep the momentum up earlier this year, and some automakers (looking at you, Subaru ) stayed on track with plans for new EVs in the US.
Plug-in hybrids also factored in as a sort of gateway drug, with Audi CEO Gernot Döllner among those looking forward to strong EV sales in that category.

EV stakeholders must smell blood in the water as Election Day 2026 approaches. With polls indicating that Trump will lose his chokehold on federal EV policy, news about EVs has been tumbling through the Intertubes over the past several weeks. Among the examples, Slate Auto opened its first showroom in Chicago, and General Motors unveiled its gen-4 EV platform .

Somewhat bizarrely, the Trump administration also contributed to the news cycle with the launch of the new “BattMan” battery collaboration earlier this week. Under the umbrella of the US Department of Energy, BattMan hooks up federal laboratories with academic and private sector partners to push the envelope on next-gen batteries for transportation applications as well as stationary energy storage.

Of course, Tesla also weighed in with its “flying car” stunt , but that was just a stunt. Over in the world of street legal EVs, Ford has been working the publicity machine to gin up interest in the forthcoming Fathom all-electric pickup truck , which is on track for volume production early next year at an MSRP starting at the affordability benchmark of $28,350 with a built-in inverter that cuts the cost of bidirectional charging , too.

The Fathom illustrates how much blood, sweat, and tears go into naming a new car. It’s a mid-sized pickup like the popular Maverick, but Ford went off in a new direction with the Fathom , considering hundreds of options over a months-long naming journey before settling on a maritime-adjacent reference to deep understanding.

title: Europe's COTY Shortlist Is An EV Clean Sweep, But China Can Only Watch
raw_summary: While this won't be the first time an EV will win Europe's COTY award, it is the first time the finalists are all electric Electric cars now account for one in three sales in Europe, but if you only looked at the shortlist announced this week for the continent's Car of the Year 2027 award, you'd be forgiven for thinking combustion power's flame had been completely snuffed out. summary: While this won't be the first time an EV will win Europe's COTY award, it is the first time the finalists are all electric Electric cars now account for one in three sales in Europe, but if you only looked at the shortlist announced this week for the continent's Car of the Year 2027 award, you'd be forgiven for thinking combustion power's flame had been completely snuffed out.
article_paragraphs: While this won't be the first time an EV will win Europe's COTY award, it is the first time the finalists are all electric

Electric cars now account for one in three sales in Europe, but if you only looked at the shortlist announced this week for the continent's Car of the Year 2027 award, you'd be forgiven for thinking combustion power's flame had been completely snuffed out. All seven of the shortlisted cars are electric — not electrified, with mild-hybrid, full hybrid, or plug-in hybrid powertrains, but pure EVs.

Electric cars have won outright several times since the first COTY award was handed out to the Rover 2000 in 1964. Nissan's Leaf was the first, in 2011, the Jaguar I-Pace came top in 2019, and the Mercedes CLA (available in both electric and hybrid form) scooped the 2026 prize. But this is the first time that EVs have taken over the entire seven-car shortlist, which 65 judges from 25 European countries arrived at after whittling down a bigger list of 38 contenders.

So which EVs made the cut? The Neue Klasse BMW iX3 , Cupra Raval, Hyundai Ioniq 3, Kia EV2, Renault Twingo, Volkswagen ID Polo, and Volvo EX60 all made it through. They beat out cars like the Renault Clio, Mercedes GLC, Polestar 5, Honda Prelude, Toyota RAV4 and Audi A2 e-tron to get there. Two particularly notable omissions are the Volkswagen T-Roc, if only because the old one was frequently top of Europe's sales charts, and the Skoda Epiq, a close cousin of the ID Polo. The judges will put the seven finalists through their paces at the Stellantis Balocco test track near Milan in November, and we'll find out the winner at the Brussels Motor Show on January 8.

The fact that Chinese cars don't appear anywhere on the shortlist is potentially even more notable than the way EVs dominate it. The China-free element wouldn't be a surprise if we were talking about the NACTOY (North American Car, Truck and Utility Vehicle of the Year) competition, because Chinese cars aren't sold in the U.S. But sales of Chinese cars are going well in Europe, accounting for one in every 10 cars sold.

Chinese EVs and hybrids did appear on the initial list of 38 cars, though. There were eight of them, including the BYD Dolphin G subcompact, sporty Denza Z9GT sedan, and the B05 and B03X from Stellantis's joint venture with Leapmotor. MG had three cars in the running, the IM5, MG4 Urban and MGS6. None of them made it through.

But if we're splitting hairs, you could argue that one Chinese car did wriggle on to the shortlist. While there are no cars from Chinese brands in the final seven, Volvo's EX60 has some very solid links to China. Volvo is owned by China's Geely, although the SUVs roll out of the brand's Torslanda, Sweden, plant.

Who's going to win? Premium and luxury cars have won on occasion, like the Porsche 928 in 1978, but historically the European judges have been drawn to more affordable models. VW's ID Polo and its Cupra Raval spinoff will have to be strong contenders if that trend continues. Don't be surprised if Renault's even cheaper Twingo comes home in top spot, just like the bigger Renault Scenic and 4 EVs did in 2024 and 2025.

title: Volkswagen hits pause on the Golf EV as it faces an ‘urgent need for action’
raw_summary: Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs. “We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.
summary: Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs. “We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.
article_paragraphs: Volkswagen has put the electric Golf on hold for now as it faces growing pressure to cut costs.

“We cannot afford to lose any time and must act quickly and decisively,” Volkswagen Group CFO and COO Arno Antlitz warned after the company reported its largest quarterly loss since the “Dieselgate” scandal in 2015 on Thursday.
VW Group’s operating loss swelled to €5.9 billion ($6.5 billion) in the third quarter because of a write-down of its Porsche stake, weak sales in China, and lower profit margins on electric vehicles.
As part of its latest cost-control efforts, Volkswagen is pausing development of the all-electric Golf at its Wolfsburg plant in Germany.

“We simply can’t afford this work right now,” VW brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said in an internal memo Reuters reviewed on Friday. The Wolfsburg plant, or the “heart of the VW brand,” is about €300 million ($334.5 million) short of its cost-cutting targets, the memo said.
Schäfer said the “decision was really not an easy one for us,” knowing what the Golf means to Wolfsburg.

The decision comes after Volkswagen’s Supervisory Board approved its restructuring strategy, “Future Plan 2030,” last month, which includes reducing its global workforce by 100,000, trimming its lineup, and closing several plants in Germany.
Volkswagen initially planned to launch the Golf EV in 2028, but Schäfer confirmed earlier this year that the electric hatch will be delayed until closer to 2030.

I said I'm always surprised to see someone actually bought a Tesla Cybertruck, for very obvious reasons . Lots of people agreed with that answer, but we love some healthy discourse here, and some folks thought I was too hard on the poor innocent Cybertruck . To that I say, "to each their own, Charlize Theron."

In all seriousness, there were literally oodles of great answers, so feel free to go back and read through the other comments that didn't make this roundup. These are a few of my favorite answers, but if yours didn't make the cut, or maybe you missed the chance to leave an answer, go ahead and leave yours in the comments below, after you read all of my thoughtful commentary, of course. These are the cars you're always surprised to see people actually bought.

My vote is the Nissan Murano CrossCabriolet. If you are not familiar, it is essentially a convertible version of the Nissan Murano. Any criticism you may have for that make or Murano base model aside, the concept of a crossover with a convertible roof baffles me. A convertible top can enhance the look of a sporty car...this does not. Since it is a crossover with higher ground clearance than a sedan, it is unlikely to benefit from the improved visibility of having the top down. I assume it provides a noisy highway ride, and in many regions in the US, winter weather likely makes it a less practical daily driver (and 19 mpg ?!). The one time I remember seeing one, the driver had the top down (of course), was wearing a button down shirt with a sweater tied around his neck (why not I guess), and was probably heading to/from the municipal golf course acting like he belonged to a country club. It's like he had less money than sense to buy this vehicle. Ultimately it feels like this weird combo of crossover and convertible, excellently captured by the name "CrossCabriolet," is a Jack of some trades, master of none.

Listen here, Jasonator, the Nissan Murano CrossCabriolet is a saint. It's one of those cars that should have never made it to production, and yet the universe was generous enough to enjoy its wackiness for four years. I say the same about the Buick Cascada later on in this blog, but I love a big four-seat convertible that stays in its lane rather than trying to be a sports car.

It's not like the Murano was ever truly marketed as an off-roader, so the CrossCabriolet didn't really have any off-road pretensions. It just lived its life as a big, squishy, top-down cruiser, and I, for one, am immensely grateful to exist in a reality where, despite being utterly silly and underbaked, Nissan sent the Murano CrossCabriolet to market. "'Tis better to have Murano CrossCabrioleted and lost than to have never Murano CrossCabrioleted at all," or whatever Socrates said.

The three-wheeled cars like the Polaris Slingshot. Give me something with none of the maneuvering benefits of a motorcycle, and like half of the comfort of a four-wheel car. No top to it so worse than a conventional convertible. I can't imagine they drive better, even as well as a conventional supercar.

Brent, I couldn't agree more. I lived with one for a week and found the experience to be so miserable that my fitness tracker kept recognizing my time behind the wheel as periods of elevated stress. And it wasn't from excitement.

title: LAPD Shuts Down Two Takeovers Before They Start
raw_summary: Street takeovers are a problem across the USA, and police departments use all sorts of tactics to deal with them. Deputies in California say their latest operation did better than most. It actually got ahead of the event and stopped two planned gatherings before the crews could get going. The LA County Sheriff's Department credits its dedicated Street Takeover Task Force for the success. The team stopped unlawful events in Cudahy and Carson recently. Most of the success appears to be thanks to organizers of these events posting about them on social media. Police say each one was intending to attract illegally modified cars and street takeover crews. Notably, police didn't reveal specifics about how they stopped the takeover, but plenty of stops and arrests might have played a role. The effort was part of a broader weekend crackdown. Deputies conducted enforcement patrols in Crescenta Valley, Carson, Compton, and unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County, and their results went well beyond disrupted weekend plans.

General Motors is going to pay $220 million to settle allegations that it had illegally collected and sold drivers' private behavior and location data to brokers , who then sold that information to insurers that used it to set and sometimes increase rates. Not a very cool move, if ya ask me. The settlement resolves claims made by 35 U.S. attorneys general over the automaker's Smart Driver program , which enrolled millions of drivers between 2016 and 2024 — when it was discontinued. Other regulators have also been reviewing GM's handling of driver data.

The automaker was accused of pitching Smart Driver as a program to help people improve their personal driving safety, but GM quickly violated their privacy by reneging on its promise not to sell their data without permission. Many folks who signed up were also enrolled in GM's OnStar safety, navigation and diagnostic service. From Reuters :
The settlement also requires GM to limit driving data it ‌collects, ⁠and obtain drivers' express consent before collecting or sharing that data.
A GM spokesperson said the settlement reinforces other steps the Detroit automaker has taken to strengthen privacy.

"Safer, more helpful and personalized experiences are enabled by connected vehicle data, and GM is committed to ​being clear about what ​information is used, how ⁠it's protected, and the choices customers have about what they share," the spokesperson said.
Insurers such as Allstate, Progressive and Berkshire Hathaway's Geico use so-called telematics in monitoring drivers' habits. They say the ​technology rewards ⁠good driving through lower premiums.

title: David Hasselhoff's Stolen KITT Replica Recovered By Interpol, Now It Could Be Yours
raw_summary: A rock tour, a theft, and an Interpol rescue later, this KITT replica is heading to auction. A talking car that drives by itself, accelerates like a rocket, and can jump over obstructions? article_paragraphs: A rock tour, a theft, and an Interpol rescue later, this KITT replica is heading to auction.

A talking car that drives by itself, accelerates like a rocket, and can jump over obstructions? Sounds like your average new BYD supercar out of China in 2026, but back in the 1980s those capabilities only existed in the fantasy world of TV's "Knight Rider," and its true star, KITT.

Up for auction in Zürich, Switzerland, the KITT replica pictured here can't jump or drive itself, and would struggle to outrun a Toyota Sienna minivan. It even looks a little shabby. But of interest to "Knight Rider" fans is its connection to crime fighter Michael Knight himself, David Hasselhoff. That and a crime backstory worthy of a "Knight Rider" script.

What started life as a humble 1982 Pontiac Firebird Trans Am was converted to KITT specification at some point during that same decade by Hollywood Productions using original Universal Pictures plans, Broad Arrow Auctions claims . KITT's signature red scanner was added to the extended nose cone, and a blackout plastic lens was fitted to the taillights to give that authentic stealthy appearance. Inside, you get an accurate KITT replica look , with dozens of 1980s LEDs, some very wonky buttons, and that iconic yoke steering wheel.

But things are less futuristic under the hood. This car has a standard 305 cu. in (5.0L) V8 that made all of 165 horsepower (167 PS) for 1982, and came with a mandatory three-speed automatic transmission. Trans Am buyers could get a four-speed manual that year, but only if they accepted a downgrade from Cross-Fire injection to a four-barrel carburetor, and just 145 hp (147 PS). Forget turbo boost and pursuit modes, buddy. These things couldn't even break 9 seconds to 60 mph (97 kph).

American fans know Hasselhoff for his acting roles, but he had a parallel career as a rock star in Europe, and documentation proves "the Hoff" used this exact replica to promote his 1985 Night Rocker album at concerts, and during TV appearances, across the continent.

The Trans Am was later sold to a Swiss record label, but its celebrity status didn't end when Hasselhoff's involvement did. Because the car was stolen at some point during the 1990s, and only returned with the help of the international sleuthing skills of Interpol. The listing doesn't say whether Devon, Michael, and April were also involved in the recovery.

Sadly, the car was returned minus some of its bespoke KITT dashboard electrics, but they've since been replaced, and the Trans Am now features all of Knight Industries' must-have interior gadgets, including a voice box, dual monitors, overhead console, and an illuminated accelerator pedal.

title: Why “ignorance is a superpower” for Antonelli in F1
raw_summary: Daniel Ricciardo believes Kimi Antonelli ’s age and innocence are what have made him so successful in the 2026 Formula 1 season. Nine victories so far in his sophomore F1 campaign have taken Antonelli to the brink of his maiden world title. article_paragraphs: Daniel Ricciardo believes Kimi Antonelli ’s age and innocence are what have made him so successful in the 2026 Formula 1 season.

Nine victories so far in his sophomore F1 campaign have taken Antonelli to the brink of his maiden world title. All the Mercedes driver needs to be crowned in Sunday’s Mexican Grand Prix is ninth place, or for neither George Russell nor Lewis Hamilton to win.
This would make the 20-year-old F1’s youngest-ever champion, beating Sebastian Vettel ’s current record by more than three years.
Ricciardo, who made his F1 debut at 22 years old and retired from the world championship at 35, believes he knows exactly how Antonelli feels – and how that makes him so strong.

“I got asked by a friend about Kimi Antonelli the other day, and I said ‘ignorance is a superpower’ – you know, ‘being young’ is what I’m really trying to say, I’m not trying to be mean to him at all,” the Australian told the Beyond The Grid podcast. “Being young is a superpower, being ignorant and not having been so exposed to the world and things like that.

“I remember my first year at Red Bull Racing ; you’re naive, you’re young, you’re ignorant. I don’t know, everything’s easy and it comes easy, and it’s just, ‘Oh wow, I’m winning, cool, I’ll just keep winning, cause I’m the best’.”

Ricciardo joined Red Bull’s main squad for the 2014 season following compatriot Mark Webber ’s retirement, teaming up with Sebastian Vettel; he unexpectedly took all three of the outfit’s victories that year, noticeably outperforming the reigning four-time world champion.

title: Used EVs Are Selling Faster Than Gas Cars or Hybrids
raw_summary: Shoppers in the market for a used car are reportedly shifting toward electric powertrains. A report from iSeeCars claims that EVs are the quickest-moving cars in the used-car market compared with their gas and hybrid counterparts, despite a higher price point than last year. The report studied over 1.5 million cars between one and five years old to find trends in the current used-car market. Between September 2025 and September 2026, used EVs saw a 9.8 percent price increase, while hybrid prices rose 4.9 percent and gas-powered prices rose less than half a percent. EVs sold for an average of $32,533 in September 2026, landing right in the middle of the more expensive hybrids at $34,476 and less expensive gas-powered vehicles at $31,954.

The report studied over 1.5 million cars between one and five years old to find trends in the current used-car market. Between September 2025 and September 2026, used EVs saw a 9.8 percent price increase, while hybrid prices rose 4.9 percent and gas-powered prices rose less than half a percent. EVs sold for an average of $32,533 in September 2026, landing right in the middle of the more expensive hybrids at $34,476 and less expensive gas-powered vehicles at $31,954.

Though EV prices are increasing, they’re moving off sales floors a lot faster than gasoline models that have stayed relatively the same price. In September 2026, used EVs averaged 41.9 days on the market, which is 13 days less than gas-powered cars. Hybrids find themselves in the middle with about 48.6 days on the market. Compared with September 2025, used EVs sold 10.1 percent faster, while gas cars saw a 19.9 percent longer sales window.

However, gas-powered cars take up the top two spots on the overall fastest-selling cars list. The Lexus IS500, which saw its last production year in 2025, took the top spot, followed by the Audi A4 Allroad, another gasoline model. The Audi Q4 e-tron Sportback sits in third place as the first EV on the list, spending an average of 29.8 days on the market. Gas-powered cars may have dominated the top two spots, but EVs still managed to sell faster overall than the gas-powered herd.

The fastest-selling EVs recorded were the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron, followed by the Toyota bZ4X, and the Lexus RZ 300e. Though not on the top-10 fastest-selling list at all, Teslas saw some of the highest price increases this year, with the Model S averaging $10,636 higher than in September 202

In terms of size, the Chinese Edge L is significantly larger than the discontinued Edge. It measures 5,011 mm (197 in) long and has a 2,950 mm (116 in) wheelbase. For context, the U.S.-spec Explorer is only 39 mm (1.5 in) longer with 75 mm (3 in) more space between the axles. The big difference between the two is that the Edge L utilizes a FWD platform, whereas the Explorer rides on a RWD longitudinal layout.

Inside, the Ford Edge L retains its three-row sever-seater layout, 27-inch 4K touchscreen, and 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster. However, the infotainment gains an upgraded Qualcomm Snapdragon 8155 chip running the Chinese-specific Ford SYNC Max software with AI integration.

The entry-level Fashion trim comes standard with the digital cockpit, panoramic sunroof, tri-zone climate control, synthetic leather upholstery, active noise cancellation, and Ford's Co-Pilot360 Level 2 driver assistance. The Supreme trim adds more premium features such as a head-up display, a B&O audio system, a 540-degree surround-view camera, as well as heated and ventilated second-row captain chairs with power leg rests and reclining function.

The powertrain lineup of the Edge L remains unchanged, with ICE and hybrid options. The turbo 2.0-liter EcoBoost four-cylinder engine is good for 249 horsepower (185 kW/252 PS) and is mated to an 8-speed automatic. The hybrid 2.0-liter version has a combined output of 275 hp (205 kW/275 PS) and is mated to an eCVT, offering a range of up to 1,188 km (738 miles) on a single tank. Both engines are available in front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive configurations.

Prices for the refreshed Ford Edge L in China start at ¥229,800 ($34,500) and top out at ¥299,800 ($45,000). By comparison, the similarly-sized Ford Explorer, starts at $40,475 in the U.S. Besides the local market, the Chinese-built Ford Edge L is also offered in select export markets like Mexico.

title: What Car Would You Lease But Never Buy?
raw_summary: When getting a new car, the age-old question is always whether it's better to buy or lease . Of course, the answer often comes down to the individual, their financial situation, and what sort of commitment they're looking for, but there's another important part of the equation: The car itself. Some cars are just better to lease than they are to buy, and that idea is what brings me to today's question. I want to know what car you would lease, but would never consider buying. What car, for one reason or another, could you stomach making a financial commitment to for two or three years, but once that time is over, have a dealership take it back off your hands for good?

article_paragraphs: When getting a new car, the age-old question is always whether it's better to buy or lease . Of course, the answer often comes down to the individual, their financial situation, and what sort of commitment they're looking for, but there's another important part of the equation: The car itself. Some cars are just better to lease than they are to buy, and that idea is what brings me to today's question.

I want to know what car you would lease, but would never consider buying. What car, for one reason or another, could you stomach making a financial commitment to for two or three years, but once that time is over, have a dealership take it back off your hands for good?

Obviously, there are plenty of reasons why some cars are better to lease than buy. Maybe an automaker is running good lease rates on a particular model. Maybe they've got a bit of a reputation for — let's say — being around for a good time, not a long time. Maybe you've done the math, and you've realized that a certain type of car (electric) is being updated so rapidly that committing to the technology of today long-term probably isn't going to pay off five or 10 years from now, so getting into a car for two or three years just makes more sense.

My pick is a simple one, and it checks two of the boxes I just mentioned: unreliability and a rapidly changing EV landscape. It's the Lucid Air. I absolutely adore the Air . There's an argument that it's the best sedan on sale today, perhaps even the best vehicle, regardless of body style. It's especially appealing if you opt for the quarter-million-dollar version, the Air Sapphire , but I won't be greedy with my choice. Unfortunately, the Sapphire is a bit unreliable , and there are several known bugs with the car's software that make it hard to justify such a big price tag. It does, however, also check the EV box.

So, while it is a fantastic car now, it probably won't be in a decade's time. And why would I want to deal with the headache and heartache of having a car that is so deeply outdated — especially when it's supposed to be software-defined? I wouldn't, and neither would you. Anyway, that's enough out of me. How about you all head on down below and let your fellow Jalops know what car you would absolutely lease but would never buy? As always, cash prizes will be given out to those who explain their answers.

raw_summary: Waymo is adding the Toyota bZ4X to its robotaxi lineup. Toyota will build a custom version of the electric SUV with the Waymo Driver integrated right on the line in Japan, and a test fleet will start operating there in 2027. It’s the first actual vehicle to come out of the partnership the two companies signed last year. And it gives Waymo a Japanese-built car for its Tokyo launch, with the UK and other markets to follow.

article_paragraphs: Waymo is adding the Toyota bZ4X to its robotaxi lineup. Toyota will build a custom version of the electric SUV with the Waymo Driver integrated right on the line in Japan, and a test fleet will start operating there in 2027.
It’s the first actual vehicle to come out of the partnership the two companies signed last year. And it gives Waymo a Japanese-built car for its Tokyo launch, with the UK and other markets to follow.

When Waymo and Toyota first announced their deal in April 2025 , it was a preliminary agreement to “explore” working together on autonomous driving, including in personally owned vehicles. Lots of intent, no product.

Now there’s a product. According to Waymo’s announcement , Toyota will produce the vehicles at its Takaoka plant in Toyota City, Aichi Prefecture, and Waymo’s self-driving hardware will be installed and integrated at that same site instead of being retrofitted somewhere else.

The robotaxi bZ4X gets a few rider-focused changes: extra rear legroom, automatic doors, a power liftgate, and ambient lighting. Waymo didn’t share sensor specs, unit volumes, or what each vehicle costs.
Operations in 2027 are about testing and validating the autonomous bZ4X fleet in Japan. The UK and “other Waymo markets” come in later years, with no dates attached.
The two companies also say they’ll keep working on autonomous tech for Toyota’s personal vehicles, plus safety projects with Woven by Toyota, the automaker’s software arm.
Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov said that “Toyota’s commitment to zero traffic accidents resonates deeply with us at Waymo.”

McLaren has already confirmed that the 750S end production in 2027 , but enthusiasts won't have to wait long for its replacement. McLaren has already confirmed that the 750S end production in 2027 , but enthusiasts won't have to wait long for its replacement. We might already know the name of the 750S' replacement and its expected horsepower, and it's all thanks to a sculpture of a bird on display in a busy London shopping district. The kiwi bird is McLaren's traditional mascot, a nod to founder Bruce McLaren's New Zealand roots, and the automaker recently placed a huge orange and black kiwi sculpture in London's Covent Garden.

But eagle-eyed Autocar spotted the lettering "McL 820" printed in orange text on the artwork, leading the UK magazine to deduce that it must be a teaser for next year's 750S replacement. If it's right, that could mean the next supercar has 809 horsepower, assuming it follows McLaren's current badge numbering system, 809 hp equating to 820 metric horses. That would put it within 10 hp of Ferrari's 819 hp (830 PS) 296 GTB, though we expect McLaren to make its power using a twin-turbocharged V8 engine, rather than a V6 like Ferrari employs. It would also make the McL 820 70 hp (70 PS) stouter than the 750S it replaces.

The numbers aren't all that's new in that name. It looks like the 750S replacement will get the "McL" prefix introduced on the McL 6GT earlier this year. The McL 6GT is a limited series $1.5 million supercar with McLaren's first manual transmission since the game-changing F1 of the 1990s. But we can't help wondering if the name will trip a few people up. In terms of pronunciation for the McL name, expect to hear a mixture of "Em-Cee-Ell" and "Muckle" references sprinkled into conversations at Cars and Coffee meets starting next year.

There's more going on at McLaren though than simply a new supercar and minor badging tweaks, though. The brand is now under the ownership of Abu Dhabi investment fund L'imad, and overhauling its entire operation and philosophy. That shift will result in McLaren finally building an SUV to rival musclebound utilities such as the Lamborghini Urus and top-spec Porsche Cayennes. McLaren is also building a second factory in the UK, and will soon assemble its engines in-house, after years of subcontracting to Ricardo.

article_paragraphs: In our transportation reporting, we rarely come across something as fun as today’s review of the Jasion Poki.

The Poki is a severely overpowered electric minibike that looks like it came from yesteryear. If the power isn’t enough, it also packs some cool tricks, and we’re not (just) talking about wheelies this time.

So taking a look at this bad boy, it just screams fun. It is really low to the ground, has a big, wide seat large enough for 2 people as long as they are under 350lbs total, and has pegs for 2 people and a basket, great for carrying a picnic and an extra helmet.

This thing is built like a tank, and it tips the scales accordingly. Getting this thing in my SUV ruptured a few discs in my back, though its compact nature means it fit quite well. Loosen the handlebars and it is downright compact. But that weight is strangely like 50lbs heavier than I would expect at close to 140lbs.

That also makes the built-in wheelies a little bit more suspect. My son, who is by now becoming an expert at wheelies, found this one to be a bit more difficult than the auto wheelies on bikes like the Anyland or new Yozma IN11.

OK so not only does this little powerhouse get you (and your friend) around town in style and it also makes wheelies a bit easier; but it also has a huge Bluetooth speaker in the back that sounds like a Harley and is all synced up with the actual controller so it sounds real.
Sure, it is a gimmick, but it is a fun one, and it might actually make the low-down bike a little safer since it is going to be out of the sight of most cars.

I love this thing. It is my favorite bike to go to the beach on (and it does well in the sand with those fat tires). But I think there are some big misses here. First of all, it has no business going over 40mph. Not only does it feel scary with those tiny wheels, but speed wobbles puts both the rider a possible second rider at significant risk here. This is a fun bike and it should top out at 20-28mph max. Keep all the torque, just cut out the power at a reasonable top speed.

There comes a point when Corvette ownership demands something more than clunky white walking shoes, jorts worn with tall socks, and the non-ironic possession of at least one of those creepy little 'Time Out' car show dolls. Certain Corvettes, especially those built in this millennium, offer performance levels that demand respect when carving up windy roads or revving at a stoplight.

The 2007 Chevy Corvette Z06 we looked at yesterday is one of those serious editions. With the largest naturally aspirated small-block ever wedged into a Corvette engine bay and a specially lightened chassis, the Z06 handily outshone its lesser brethren. Our car was also touted as having "tasteful updates" and would be accompanied in the sale with a slew of maintenance and repair receipts.

A bit of research showed that the seller's $47,000 asking price is at the bottom of the Z06 market, making it an intriguing opportunity. While the car's desirability and value were both noted by many in the comments, that price inexplicably fell by a 68% 'No Dice' loss in the vote. That's a bit of a head-scratcher, because, honestly, these cars ain't gonna get any cheaper.

Recently, popular YouTuber Rich Benoit, aka "Rich Rebuilds," aka "Massachusetts Man," posted a video detailing a 2023 Polestar 2 Performance he bought at a salvage auction for around $3,000. The car, an ex-Hertz rental with around 80K on the clock, was listed with undercarriage damage and as not running. Aesthetically, however, the car looked pretty great for a former "rent it and dent it." Rich diagnosed several issues with the car, including a coolant leak, a missing fireman's loop, and, puzzlingly, a broken rear shock mount. Having fixed all of those issues, the car ran and, according to Rich, went like stink. The total outlay for the Polestar was under five grand, making it a relative bargain despite the salvage title.

This is an important fact, as it sets the baseline for how much the value of Polestar products has dropped in recent months. The cars, built by automaker Geely in China, have recently been in the news because the current administration has banned them from being sold in the States — based on the brand's Chinese ownership percentage. It's been pandemonium for Polestar dealers, but it may be a boon for used-market buyers looking for a deal on a decent EV.

This 2024 Polestar 2 Long Range looks to be more than just decent. This model is a significant update over the earlier 2021-2023 cars, offering a larger battery, dual motors with more performance, and a standard package (Pilot Pack) that offers adaptive cruise control, lane assist, and parking aids.

Together, the front and rear motors produce 421 horsepower and a stonking 545 pound-feet of torque, available from zero rpm. Juicing those motors is a 78 kWh under-floor battery. It can charge at up to 200 kW for reasonably quick refueling and offers around 275 miles of range if treated with care. The electricity to charge that battery and propel the Polestar is getting increasingly more expensive (like everything), but on average, it's still a heck of a lot cheaper than buying gas for any similar-spec car or truck. According to the ad, this Polestar has a clean title and comes with a mere 18,250 miles on the ticker.

raw_title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid's Silence Speaks Volumes
title: 2027 Nissan Rogue Hybrid's Silence Speaks Volumes
raw_summary: Standing out from the crowd is never easy, especially in the compact crossover segment . Whether it's the Honda CR-V, Hyundai Tucson, Chevy Equinox or the mighty Toyota RAV4, all compact crossovers sort of look the same, are similarly sized, have the same sort of tech, and usually drive the same, too. However, with the 2027 Rogue Hybrid , Nissan is looking to switch up the game by leaning on its trick e-Power series hybrid drivetrain that gives the Rogue a driving experience unlike any hybrid vehicle I've ever driven before — and more importantly, it's unlike any gas-powered crossover I've ever driven. I mean, hell, it even has one-pedal driving. The name of the game when it comes to the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is peace and quiet. Throughout my introduction to the car, Nissan's designers and engineers emphasized how silent the Rogue Hybrid's cabin is and the lack of any sort of serious engine noise, and those claims were backed up over the 70-ish miles of testing I did on a rare rainy day in Southern California. Add in a simple yet comfortable cabin, a decent amount of tech, thoughtful safety features, solid build quality, competitive efficiency, and soft looks that buck the trend of simulated machismo that is all the rage these days, and Nissan delivered a package that's impressive as hell.

article_paragraphs: Standing out from the crowd is never easy, especially in the compact crossover segment . Whether it's the Honda CR-V, Hyundai Tucson, Chevy Equinox or the mighty Toyota RAV4, all compact crossovers sort of look the same, are similarly sized, have the same sort of tech, and usually drive the same, too. However, with the 2027 Rogue Hybrid , Nissan is looking to switch up the game by leaning on its trick e-Power series hybrid drivetrain that gives the Rogue a driving experience unlike any hybrid vehicle I've ever driven before — and more importantly, it's unlike any gas-powered crossover I've ever driven. I mean, hell, it even has one-pedal driving.

The name of the game when it comes to the 2027 Rogue Hybrid is peace and quiet. Throughout my introduction to the car, Nissan's designers and engineers emphasized how silent the Rogue Hybrid's cabin is and the lack of any sort of serious engine noise, and those claims were backed up over the 70-ish miles of testing I did on a rare rainy day in Southern California. Add in a simple yet comfortable cabin, a decent amount of tech, thoughtful safety features, solid build quality, competitive efficiency, and soft looks that buck the trend of simulated machismo that is all the rage these days, and Nissan delivered a package that's impressive as hell.
Full Disclosure: Nissan flew me out to Santa Barbara, California, put me up in a lovely hotel and fed me all so I could check out the 2027 Rogue Hybrid.

The Rogue Hybrid drives like nothing else on the road today in America, simply because the closest thing to it in our country is actually a train. Unlike every other non-plug-in hybrid on the market, which are parallel hybrid systems with gas and electric motors that work in tandem to motivate the drive wheels, the Rogue Hybrid's e-Power drivetrain is a series hybrid .

That means the 148-horsepower turbocharged 1.5-liter inline-three cylinder motor under the hood is only responsible for charging up the 1.67-kWh battery, and it has absolutely no mechanical connection to the front or rear wheels. That motor also achieves 42% thermal efficiency, which is damn good for an internal combustion engine. It might be the same size as the normal Rogue's engine, but Nissan engineers tell me it's a completely different motor.

The wheels are actually powered by electric motors on the front and rear axles, meaning all-wheel drive is standard. Up front, the motor produces 202 hp and 243 pound-feet of torque; the less-powerful rear motor makes 134 hp and 144 lb-ft of torque. All in all, the system generates 225 hp, which is enough to rocket the 4,065-pound Rogue Hybrid from 0-60 mph in just 6.4 seconds. Nissan claims that's the quickest in its class, and that's incredibly important if you're the kind of compact crossover buyer who cares about that sort of thing. While that is very exciting, something that may be a bit of a letdown is the gas mileage the Rogue Hybrid achieves.

Nissan says the new crossover will get 41 mpg city, 36 mpg highway and 38 mpg combined. Sure, those are respectable numbers, but they're certainly behind the now-hybrid-only RAV4's 46 mpg city, 39 mpg highway and 42 mpg combined. The Rogue Hybrid asks what comfort and refinement are worth to you, because the experience behind the wheel of Nissan's vehicle is a far more pleasant one. It's much quieter and far more upscale than the Toyota, and the rest of its competitors. Plus, in day-to-day life, the near-EV-like driving experience it delivers is far more pleasant than the admittedly rattly four-popper noises of Toyota's hybrid system. Adding in the fact there's no transmission to shift makes things even smoother — no, there blissfully isn't even a CVT. My time with the Rogue Hybrid made me very curious as to how this powertrain technology would feel in a more luxurious application, like an Infiniti, where comfort is key and efficiency isn't nearly as important. I've got a feeling it would be rather lovely.

Stepping on the gas pedal gave me the exact sort of acceleration feel I'd get from a conventional electric vehicle, just with the added hum of that three-cylinder in the distance. Nissan did a solid job of muffling its noise as much as possible, so for the most part, I didn't even notice it was running.

McLaren: Leonardo Fornaroli for Lando Norris Red Bull: Ayumu Iwasa for Max Verstappen Mercedes: Frederik Vesti for George Russell Alpine: Gabriele Mini for Franco Colapinto Williams: Luke Browning for Alex Albon Racing Bulls: Nikola Tsolov for Liam Lawson Haas: Ryo Hirakawa for Esteban Ocon Audi: Freddie Slater for Gabriel Bortoleto Aston Martin: Jak Crawford for Lance Stroll Cadillac: Colton Herta for Valtteri Bottas

There are some familiar FP1 names there who have already driven in 2026, but Mexico is probably the most interesting roster of the season, with three names in particular standing out as significant in F1 driver market terms…
Cadillac believes Colton Herta is now just one point away from finally earning the 40 he needs to successfully apply for an F1 superlicence.
That's if he can successfully complete the mandated 100 kilometres of running in FP1 when he takes over Valtteri Bottas's Cadillac on Friday.
There's no guarantee of that given how tough the conditions are in Mexico and the various reliability issues F1 newcomer Cadillac has encountered.

But even if he doesn't get that 100km, Cadillac will ensure he ticks off that last point somewhere else. The team has already satisfied the rookie driver rule; it's only putting Herta in the car for FP1 in Mexico to make sure he gets to the 40 points.

article_paragraphs: BMW is giving its M cars yellow DRLs, but this M5 prototype didn't get the message

BMW's new 3 Series is only weeks away from arriving in dealerships, and it looks like the facelifted 5 Series and M5 won't be too far behind. Fresh spy shots from Germany show the latest prototypes of the hot PHEV midsize sedan are fitted with production lights, a sign that a debut isn't far off.

Each of the two headlight bodies has a pair of slim LED DRLs arranged horizontally, rather than diagonally, as on the new 3 Series and electric i3. And zooming in on the images appears to show LED headlight units located under each DRL. BMW's big 7 Series sedan and X7 have split headlights treatments, but the 5 is sticking with a more conventional layout.

There is one important change, though, still to come to this M5's lighting setup before its ready for an official reveal. BMW has begun fitting yellow DRLs to mark out its M cars, like the new M350 , but this car has white ones. That suggests they're from the regular 5 Series, which is getting the same facelift treatment.

This prototype is still wearing heavy disguise over the kidney grille area and down the center of the hood. But now that the 3 Series is out, we have a good idea of what we'll find underneath that camo when the M5 makes its debut, probably in the first half of next year. That plate riveted to the hood must hide a deep gulley that culminates in BMW's trademark roundel badge, and the visor-like face of the smaller sedan will be replicated.

We're not seeing any obvious changes to this M5's rear, but the taillights are sure to get a subtly different LED graphic to help distinguish the car wearing them as a facelift – or what brand fans know as Life Cycle Impulse (LCI) – model.

And the M5's trademark quad exhaust tailpipe arrangement isn't going anywhere. That's been an M5 staple since the introduction of the first V8 M5, the E39, back in 1999 . The M5 switched to V10 power after that, before coming back to a V8, this time with twin turbochargers. And the current G90-code M5 that arrived in 2024 added plug-in hybrid assistance.

Going the hybrid route added a staggering 1,045 lbs (474 kg) to the M5's curb weight, but it also pushed total output to 717 horsepower (727 PS). Will this new-look M5 and its M5 Touring wagon twin get more ponies? BMW tends not to mess with its M powertrains at facelift time, so we're not banking on it. But we wouldn't be surprised if it leveraged BMW's clever new battery technology to improve on a 38-mile (62 km) WLTP range. That figure looks off the pace in an era of hybrids like the Range Rover Sport that can do over 70 miles (113 km) on a charge.

title: Why 'motocross' Sepang wasn't fixed
raw_summary: Multiple MotoGP riders have expressed concerns about the state of the Sepang International Circuit’s asphalt ahead of this weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix. A track already in need of resurfacing was further damaged by this month’s replacement Formula 1 race - running as the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' in lieu of a race at the country's actual Sakhir track - to the point where it has now, according to some racers, become borderline dangerous to ride on.

article_paragraphs: Multiple MotoGP riders have expressed concerns about the state of the Sepang International Circuit’s asphalt ahead of this weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix.

A track already in need of resurfacing was further damaged by this month’s replacement Formula 1 race - running as the 'Bahrain Grand Prix' in lieu of a race at the country's actual Sakhir track - to the point where it has now, according to some racers, become borderline dangerous to ride on.

Last resurfaced 10 years ago, the track was due to receive new asphalt ahead of this year’s MotoGP event, but delays to logistics caused by the geopolitical situation in the Middle East saw this work pushed back.
And the high downforce generated by F1 cars has caused considerable further degradation of the track at a number of key corners.

The unexpected arrival of F1 also saw remedial work planing the straights, in an attempt to remove bumps - which appears to have exacerbated the situation in other regards. The track is now shedding stones due to the forces generated by the bikes as they accelerate.

MotoGP had a similar issue at the second round of the 2026 season at the inaugural Brazilian Grand Prix in Goiania, where the main race on Sunday was cut in distance at the last minute as the track started to crumble during the Moto2 and Moto3 races.

And, speaking to riders after the opening day of practice on Friday, a number were less than happy that their request to resurface after testing hadn’t been accomplished given the state of the asphalt right now.
“The asphalt is, pardon my French, f**ked,” Jack Miller told the media.

The 60-year-old Swiss was part of the Sauber organisation - which Audi took over to enter F1 - since even before its grand prix debut in 1993.
He went from being a mechanic there, with its factory-backed Mercedes operation in World Sportscars, to serving as team manager for much of Sauber's time in F1.

Team founder Peter Sauber stepped away from the team in 2012 and retired in 2016, as Finn Rausing's Longbow Finance took over the team. Zehnder retained a senior role then, but shortly following Audi's takeover he transitioned to a factory-based role.
He will now exit the project entirely "following the restructuring of operations ahead of the 2027 season".
Zehnder, who had worked at 601 consecutive F1 grands prix, "has been a mentor to hundreds of team members and drivers who have passed through Hinwil over the years", Audi wrote.
"We thank him for 39 years of outstanding service and wish him all the very best for the future."

title: Why F1 teams and manufacturers face more unknowns in Mexico than ever
raw_summary: At 2,286 metres above sea level, the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez is by far the highest-altitude venue on the Formula 1 calendar. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways. Firstly, the lower air density means that the power unit, and particularly the turbo, is put under considerable strain in Mexico. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways. Firstly, the lower air density means that the power unit, and particularly the turbo, is put under considerable strain in Mexico.
article_paragraphs: At 2,286 metres above sea level, the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez is by far the highest-altitude venue on the Formula 1 calendar. This naturally means thinner air, which presents a unique challenge at the Mexican Grand Prix for teams and manufacturers in two ways.

Firstly, the lower air density means that the power unit, and particularly the turbo, is put under considerable strain in Mexico. At altitude, there are fewer oxygen molecules per cubic metre, meaning the turbo has to work harder to get the same amount of oxygen into the engine as it would at sea level.

The turbo has to spin considerably faster to achieve the required boost pressure and airflow, which presents a challenge not only in terms of outright performance but also reliability, with the turbo operating at significantly higher temperatures than under normal conditions.

This is always a challenge in Mexico and also explains why George Russell pointed so clearly towards Ferrari as the favourites during Thursday's press conference, given that the Scuderia is widely known in the paddock to have a smaller turbo than many of its rivals. A smaller turbine wheel has less mass and inertia, allowing the turbo to spool up more quickly after the driver presses the throttle.

This helps to keep turbo lag to a minimum, and that is precisely what promises to be a hugely important factor this weekend. In 2026, this challenge has become considerably greater than before because the MGU-H has been removed and can no longer assist in counteracting turbo lag.

“Last year, we had the MGU-H, so we had some support from MGU-H, but this year we don't have the MGU-H anymore, so that makes it quite challenging,” Honda’s chief engineer Shintaro Orihara said when asked about the challenges by Autosport.

“For example, even just in idle conditions, we had MGU-H support to get enough boost pressure, but this year we don't have any support even in idle conditions. That is a big difference from last year and therefore turbo lag is the most interesting and important topic at this track. I think that is not only the case for Honda, but for all manufacturers. They will all struggle with turbo lag at this track.”

Besides turbo lag, there is another important factor: the extent to which the engine’s power output is affected. If manufacturers cannot achieve the desired level of turbo boost in general, Honda says this could also have consequences for how it has to run the internal combustion engine – in other words, in the worst-case scenario, with a lower power output.

"Together with the doctors, we decided all together to not continue and wait tonight and see tomorrow morning, because, at the moment, if he [Martin] wants to make the laptime, to make the time attack, it's for him difficult to manage the force," Aprilia team manager Paolo Bonora explained to MotoGP.com.

Q2 by virtue of a top-10 spot would have been a monumental longshot for Martin anyway, whereas for Marquez it looked a foregone conclusion - despite him crashing at the final corner in the early phase of the session.
He bounced back from this to head his Sepang-specialist brother Alex by 0.109s at the conclusion of the session, despite sacrificing the opportunity of one final run on a fresh soft rear.

Trackhouse Aprilia rider Ai Ogura had looked off for much of the day but uncharacteristically came alive when it came to single-lap attempts, moving up to third, ahead of the lead KTM of Pedro Acosta and VR46 Ducati rider Fabio Di Giannantonio.
Marco Bezzecchi (Aprilia), Enea Bastianini (Tech3 KTM), Maverick Vinales (Tech3 KTM), Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) and the returning Joan Mir (Honda) picked up the remaining Q2 spots.

The news sent LiveWire’s stock plunging more than 40% on Thursday morning as the company withdrew its full-year financial guidance.
article_paragraphs: Harley-Davidson-born electric motorcycle maker LiveWire has issued a troubling warning about its financial future, announcing that it has substantial doubt about its ability to continue operating as a going concern. The news sent LiveWire’s stock plunging more than 40% on Thursday morning as the company withdrew its full-year financial guidance.

The announcement comes despite some signs of improving sales, with LiveWire reporting a 38% increase in third-quarter revenue to $7.9 million and a 21% rise in motorcycle unit sales. However, the company continues to burn through cash, reporting a net loss of $18.6 million for the quarter.
LiveWire’s cash reserves have also dwindled significantly, falling from $82.8 million at the end of 2025 to just $39.9 million as of September 30, 2026.

The company has now formed a special restructuring committee to explore potential financing arrangements, strategic partnerships, investments, or even a sale. It also withdrew its previous guidance projecting a $70 million to $80 million operating loss for 2026.
The financial warning comes at a particularly pivotal moment for LiveWire, which is preparing to launch its most affordable electric motorcycles yet.

The upcoming LiveWire S4 Honcho series represents a major departure from the company’s existing premium electric motorcycles, offering smaller, lighter, and significantly more affordable models designed to attract a much broader audience of riders with a starting price below US $5,000.

The lower prices could dramatically increase LiveWire’s sales volumes, especially as the company attempts to move beyond the relatively small market for high-dollar electric motorcycles. The Honcho lineup is also expected to help lower the barrier to entry for new riders, with approachable electric motorcycles that eliminate the complexity of clutch and gear shifting.
LiveWire is also preparing to showcase its latest developments at EICMA in Milan next week , where it is expected to display new models and further expand its upcoming electric motorcycle lineup.

article_paragraphs: Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker to provide electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in international markets, including the U.K.

Under the partnership announced Friday, Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. (The electric vehicle is now known as the BZ in the North American market)

The autonomous bZ4X vehicles will initially be tested in Japan, where Waymo intends to eventually operate a robotaxi service. But the intent is to deploy these vehicles in other right-hand driving countries such as the U.K. Waymo has been testing its autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London for months and plans to launch a robotaxi service there once it receives the necessary permits.

The announcement comes 18 months after Toyota and Waymo signed a preliminary agreement to explore the development and deployment of an autonomous vehicle platform. At the time, the agreement fell into the “let’s see what happens” category, with language vague enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation.
For now, the partnership looks more like a conventional vehicle supplier deal that helps Waymo fill specific regional needs while adding a new model to its robotaxi portfolio.
But the partnership could go beyond robotaxis. The companies said they will continue to look at bringing Waymo’s autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles.

Toyota and Waymo also announced plans to look at other future “initiatives” that would use “insights from Waymo’s real-world operations” to improve safety for other road users. What that might mean is unclear, although Hiroki Nakajima, executive vice president of Toyota and a board member, provided some clues.

“This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still,” he said in a statement.

summary: The ALSO TM-B is one of the most technologically interesting new e-bikes to hit the road in years, largely because it does away with one of the most fundamental parts of a bicycle: the mechanical connection between the pedals and rear wheel. With only copper wires connecting the pedals to the rear wheel, the TM-B is one of the most revolutionary new e-bikes in years.
article_paragraphs: The ALSO TM-B is one of the most technologically interesting new e-bikes to hit the road in years, largely because it does away with one of the most fundamental parts of a bicycle: the mechanical connection between the pedals and rear wheel. With only copper wires connecting the pedals to the rear wheel, the TM-B is one of the most revolutionary new e-bikes in years.
But that raises an obvious question. What happens when the battery dies?
One early Launch Edition owner, Aaron Draczynski, decided to find out by deliberately running his TM-B down toward empty to see whether ALSO’s drive-by-wire system would leave him stranded.
He shared the experience on YouTube, discovering that the answer is surprisingly complicated – and involves something called “Infinite Turtle Mode.”

Unlike a conventional e-bike, where the rider’s pedaling mechanically turns the rear wheel through a chain or belt, the ALSO TM-B uses a pedal-by-wire drivetrain. Pedaling generates electricity, while the rear wheel is driven electrically.

That arrangement enables all sorts of interesting features, including electronically simulated gearing and the Launch Edition’s massive Level 10 boost mode, which can multiply rider input by up to 10 times.
But it also means there’s no traditional drivetrain to fall back on when the battery runs out.

The owner began his experiment at 31% charge and quickly watched the bike progressively restrict its maximum assist as the battery drained closer to empty. From 23% to 13%, the maximum boost dropped from Level 8 to Level 5 as it began conserving battery.

But while he has cleared that first hurdle, his weekend got off to a mixed start in Friday morning practice at Sepang.
The good news was that he managed to complete the full session, covering 12 laps across multiple runs, and going back out again for the practice starts at the end of the session.

That mileage and his Aprilia team talking confidently about its strategy for Martin through the weekend immediately suggested he was expecting to pass the mandatory medical check after the session - which he duly did half an hour later.

Limiting the title fight damage looks tough, though. While Martin improved from being four seconds off the pace on his tentative first run, he was still 1.835s down and 20th fastest at the end of the session, so will need to find substantially more pace to have a shot at scoring significant points.
And the identity of the pacesetter was bad news for Martin too, with his title rival Marc Marquez's Ducati a comfortable fastest by 0.474s over Martin's Aprilia team-mate Marco Bezzecchi.

KTM's Pedro Acosta matched Bezzecchi's time in third, while Acosta's stablemates Enea Bastianini and Brad Binder used fresher tyres to go fourth and fifth at the end, just as sixth-placed Franco Morbidelli (VR46 Ducati) did.
While one of Aprilia's injured duo looks set to continue with the weekend, the other was ruled out during practice one.

title: Off-Grid Power In A Briefcase: The Goal Zero Boulder 100

The early foundations of Goal Zero were established back in 2007, when Robert Workman, who had owned Utah’s Provo Craft & Novelty for 30 years, founded a nonprofit called TIFIE Humanitarian to help Congolese villagers run their own small businesses. When out in the field, his team had nowhere to charge their equipment, and a simple 90 watt solar panel he priced in the nearby city of Kinshasa cost $2,000 USD.

As a result of this, Workman went out and had his own system built. The first version was called the GoBe, it paired a battery with a solar panel and an LED light, and it was being tested in Congolese villages by 2008. It was a simple arrangement and a full day of charging in the sun would give hours of light at night, plus power for other small devices.

Goal Zero launched as a Utah-based company in mid-2009 with the Escape 150, a 13 lb power pack, and sales took off from there. In 2013 it ranked 9th on the Inc. 500 list of the country’s fastest-growing private companies, with an incredible three-year growth rate of 16,981%.

The company’s portable Nomad solar panels debuted in 2011, and then in 2012 came the 103 lb Yeti 1250 power station, which the company says sold out within a day and a half. NRG Energy bought the company in 2014, and lithium-battery Yetis arrived in 2017. BioLite acquired Goal Zero from NRG in April 2025. The company still operates from Draper, Utah, and it now has dozens of products on offer, and they ship around the world.

The Boulder 100 Solar Briefcase from Goal Zero it’s a folding two-panel solar system that provides up to 100 watts, or 50 watts per panel. It was developed to give campers the toughness of a rigid glass solar panel in a size that packs flat and fits neatly in a car trunk.

This policy will ensure that home buyers have the information that they need to make informed choices when making what is often the most important financial decision in their lives,” said Bethany Cotton, Conservation Director with Cascadia Wildlands . “The vote is an important step forward to tackling building emissions, reducing energy costs, and meeting the City’s Climate Recovery Ordinance goals to reduce emissions by 50% by 2030.”

article_paragraphs: Eugene, Oregon — In a 6-1 vote on Wednesday, October 28th , the Eugene City Council adopted the Residential Energy Performance Disclosure Requirement ordinance , a policy commonly referred to as a Home Energy Score requirement. The vote places Eugene among four other Oregon cities , Portland, Hillsboro, Milwaukie and Bend, that have similar Home Energy Score ordinances. The vote comes in the midst of a larger trend of cities adopting a variety of policies to aid community members navigating home retrofits and efficiency upgrades as support for building electrification grows in Oregon, and nationwide in the face of efforts to undermine existing climate policy at the Federal level.

“We applaud the City Council for taking this common sense step and establishing a home energy score requirement in Eugene. This policy will ensure that home buyers have the information that they need to make informed choices when making what is often the most important financial decision in their lives,” said Bethany Cotton, Conservation Director with Cascadia Wildlands . “The vote is an important step forward to tackling building emissions, reducing energy costs, and meeting the City’s Climate Recovery Ordinance goals to reduce emissions by 50% by 2030.”

The adoption of the ordinance is the first major step from the City to reduce building emissions since the Ninth Circuit’s April 2023 decision on the Berkley building electrification requirement, which invalidated the City’s February 2023 residential building electrification ordinance. The passage of this policy in Eugene also marks more than 1 million Oregonians living in a jurisdiction with a Home Energy Score disclosure policy, representing nearly 1 in 4 Oregon residents (24.4%).

“The Ninth Circuit’s disastrous decision in 2023 set Eugene, and cities across the region, back for years on climate action and energy efficiency. While this policy is just a small step, it is a critical signal that the City is ready to begin moving decisively to regaining lost time and transitioning away from polluting fossil fuels,” said Dylan Plummer, Deputy Director of the Sierra Club’s Clean Heat Campaign . “We look forward to supporting Eugene and other local governments to continue to push the ball forward on common sense policies to require building decarbonization.”

The ordinance requires that a home energy score assessment be conducted and posted when a home is listed for sale. These assessments review the average energy cost of a home, evaluating existing appliances, heating systems, windows, doors and insulation, as well as the climate emissions associated with the home, and score the house’s energy use on a scale of one to ten. The reports include recommendations for how to improve a home’s energy efficiency and reduce emissions, and include key information about existing incentives and subsidies at the local, state and federal level.

“Eugene Water and Electric Board customers can access significant incentives to support home electrification and energy efficiency including zero interest loans and cash subsidies for weatherization and heat pumps for space and water heating. Sadly, these programs are deeply underutilized because many folks are not aware they exist,” said Meredith Tufts, Coalition Coordinator with the Fossil Free Eugene Coalition . “The Home Energy Score requirement will ensure that every new home owner has the information they need to take advantage of these programs to reduce their energy bills and climate pollution.

article_paragraphs: You're looking at the first hybrid vehicle to compete in Score World Desert Championship's top Trophy Truck class,

We already knew Honda was planning to make its Passport "more masculine," but we had no idea this midsize SUV could become an off-road beast. No, it may not be as cool as a Baja-ready classic Porsche 911 , but Honda gave this rig an engine derived from an endurance racing prototype with a total power output of 1,300 hp (969 kW) — and its sights are set on an overall Baja 1000 victory. None of this is very shocking given that the truck comes from Honda Racing .

Honda's new Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck will debut at the 2026 SEMA Show, and it was developed with Mason Motorsports. Menzies Motorsports is also a partner, and two-time Baja 1000 winner Bryce Menzies will drive it in Score World Desert Championship's top Trophy Truck class, where Honda says it will be the first hybrid vehicle to compete in this class. This isn't your mom's Passport, so let's talk a little about the racing technology under this trophy truck.

Today's Trophy Trucks leverage 9.0-liter V8s. Honda says that its 2.4-liter V6-based powertrain will make more power. The engine uses a pair of turbochargers and an 800-volt hybrid system to help it achieve its somewhat wild 1,300 hp figure. Interestingly, the V6 shares very close ties with the engine in Acura's ARX-06 GTP race car , giving it some endurance racing credentials, including victories at Daytona and Sebring. That said, surviving Baja will present a different set of challenges.

The hybrid system here is bespoke and a direct product of HRC's work. The battery uses a previous-generation Formula 1-style pouch cell inside a carbon fiber case. Assembly and validation all take place within a clean room at the brand's Santa Clarita headquarters. Of course, the battery is just one piece of the overall system.

Honda says the truck also features brake-by-wire systems on each axle, adaptive traction control, and what it's calling AI power deployment. Proprietary software ties together the powertrain, chassis, and energy management, with adjustments possible during the race. Honda hasn't detailed the battery's capacity or how much power the electric side contributes.

The rear-mounted engine mates to Mason-developed five-speed transmission, and the all-wheel drive setup uses two rear driveshafts, with individual angled gearsets at the rear wheels replacing a conventional ring-and-pinion arrangement. Up front, portal gearsets at the hubs help provide ground clearance. As the photos make clear, this isn't a simple build.

If there's anything here that hints at the production Passport outside of the name, it's very selective sections of the body. Each panel is carbon fiber to save weight. Deep channels behind the front wheels manage airflow, while high-mounted exhaust outlets sit among fins behind the cockpit. Honda also shaped the cab to channel air toward a cooler mounted low and far back in the truck.

title: The Zombie Engine: How Brussels Bureaucrats Are Breathing False Life Into Combustion
raw_summary: If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. But in the EU Parliament, this fiction is being drafted into law. If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine, watched toxic exhaust billow from the tailpipe, and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. Yet inside the corridors of the European Parliament, this exact fiction is being drafted into law.
summary: If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. But in the EU Parliament, this fiction is being drafted into law. If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine, watched toxic exhaust billow from the tailpipe, and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at.
article_paragraphs: If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. But in the EU Parliament, this fiction is being drafted into law.

If you poured rapeseed oil into a combustion engine, watched toxic exhaust billow from the tailpipe, and declared it a “zero-emission vehicle,” you would be laughed at. Yet inside the corridors of the European Parliament, this exact fiction is being drafted into law.

Under heavy pressure from the fossil fuel lobby and legacy carmakers, EU lawmakers are preparing to endorse a bizarre new regulatory beast: the VEEF, or “Vehicle Exclusively running on Eligible Fuels.” In plain English, these are standard combustion-engine cars promised to run exclusively on liquid biofuels or e-fuels. In exchange for that promise, Brussels plans to grant them a legal tailpipe emission score of zero.

It is regulatory alchemy at its worst. Cloaked in the seductive language of “technological neutrality,” this proposal creates an escape hatch for an obsolete technology, all while setting up ordinary European drivers for an expensive logistical nightmare.
It is just another desperate tactic to extend the life of the combustion engine by any means possible.

To understand the absurdity of the biofuel car, look at what actually happens in the engine. It’s still the exact same combustion. A piston firing on biofuels produces the same toxic cocktail of nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, and fine particulates that has choked European cities for decades. Labeling these cars “zero-emission” launders the pollution through a regulatory loophole and continues to foster emission-induced pathology.

Nor does it save the climate. The average biofuel blend available today delivers a modest 20% to 40% emissions saving compared to fossil fuels. When you factor in the indirect land-use change of first-generation crop biofuels ploughing up forests to grow food for engines, crop-based biofuel cars actually emit 23% more greenhouse gases than a standard petrol car.

Biofuel cars are being sold to the public under the guise of affordability, yet running them is punishingly expensive. Hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) biodiesel costs around €13 per 100 kilometers to run, compared to roughly €7 for an equivalent electric vehicle. Pushing drivers toward these cars locks households into volatile, high fuel costs at the exact moment renewable electricity prices and battery costs are tumbling.
